items.body: Review by VianaProghead — Review N� 981Tangerine Dream is a progressive electronic rock band that was founded in Berlin, Germany in 1967 by Edgar Froese. Initially the band was formed as The Ones in 1965. Tangerine Dream is one of the electronic pioneers with a very extensive and amazing career. The work of them comprises several and different phases all over the years. The initial phase also called The Pink Years is the phase that is of interest for this review. As its name indicates, this is a musical phase a bit influenced by Pink Floyd. The albums that belong to that phase are the first four studio albums of Tangerine Dream, "Electronic Meditation" from 1970, "Alpha Centauri" from 1971, "Zeit" from 1972 and "Atem" from 1973.So, their initial phase began with an avant-garde and herb-rocking debut work, perhaps misleadingly titled "Electronic Meditation", because it's more a krautrock than an electronic work. In reality, it was only on their second studio album "Alpha Centauri" that the synthesizers came into play. Until then they managed to play without electronic instruments. Besides, the line up on "Electronic Meditation" isn't what is considered the classic line up of Tangerine Dream. In reality, it was only on their third studio work "Zeit" that appeared what is now considered the best line up of the band, Edgar Froese, Christopher Franke and Peter Baumann, because on their second effort "Alpha Centauri", Bauman wasn't present yet. So, "Electronic Meditation" appears to be quite a polarizing album between fans, due to that. After this album, each member went his own way, and each went on to be a renowned krautrock artist in their own way."Electronic Meditation" strongly deviates from all the other albums of the huge Tangerine Dream's catalogue. As I mentioned above, it's very ironic that "Electronic Meditation" was the only Tangerine Dream's album released in the 70's where its title didn't fit at all. It's neither electronic music made by synthesizers or meditative. The album consists apparently of experimental noises without a clear direction and purpose, performed with classic rock instruments. Nothing less representative could have been released as the debut of an electronic progressive act. In reality, this is a real rock album made with rock instruments. It's actually krautrock, the musical style invented by the German musicians in the late 60's and in the early 70's. "Electronic Meditation" is quite similar to "A Saucerful Of Secrets" and "Ummagumma" by Pink Floyd. Still, I also noticed the kind of music that Schulze later on would record with Ash Ra Tempel after he had left Tangerine Dream. Sometimes I even hear some hints of Jimi Hendrix, but also from their compatriots of Amon D��l, another krautrock German band from those days, one the best and most famous too."Electronic Meditation" has five tracks. The album starts with "Geburt (Genesis)", which is a track dominated by Schnitzler's scratchy creaking cello, combined with wild drumming and furious flute sounds performed by their guest, Keyserling. After a while something like a rhythm develops, but as soon as this is the case, the piece is already over and it goes straight and abruptly into its second track. The fittingly titled "Reise Durch Ein Brennendes Gehirn (Journey Through A Burning Brain)" begins as a freeform piece, then the organ enters with mighty tones, and finally the piece develops into a garish guitar orgy. This track encapsulates the whole krautrock vibe and it's a perfect example of crunchy rock and roll. This is probably the highlight of "Electronic Meditation". The pounding drums and acid guitar continue for "Kalter Rauch (Cold Smoke)". It begins with quiet organ sounds, which are repeatedly interrupted by short outbursts of chaos. Then the cello scrapes again, and snappy drums come and go, and another relentless psychedelic guitar attack ensues. I think it was mostly Pink Floyd that gave the inspiration to this track with its lengthy guitar/organ freak-outs. "Asche Zu Asche (Ashes To Ashes)" feels almost conventional compared to the rest of the album with a consistent rhythm and a halfway recognizable melody. The piece grows more and more furious with more distorted guitar over lazy cymbal heavy backbeat and, then suddenly, fades out. It reminds me a bit of The Doors. The concluding "Auferstehung (Resurrection)" begins with an almost solemn organ melody, to which a narrator declares a true incomprehensible text that was recorded backwards. In the further course, the theme of the opening track is taken up.Conclusion: Tangerine Dream is the best and most important electronic progressive act of the 70's and of all time, and they would over the decade make some of my all-time favourite music. Tangerine Dream is, next to Kraftwerk, the most well-known electronic formation in Germany. And just like them, they began almost entirely non-electronically. The first Tangerine Dream's album is quite a refreshing and experimentally quirky affair, quite different from the works that both Schulze and Froese later released. The five tracks are certainly worth listening to. I think the music here is probably better digested for many people than some of the material on their earlier real electronic albums. Besides, "Electronic Meditation" is a nice way to discover how Tangerine Dream started their career. And, all in all, the music on this album is probably a pleasant and interesting surprise, especially for those who are huge fans of the krautrock style of music.Prog is my Ferrari. Jem Godfrey (Frost*)
items._cn_summary: 这是Tangerine Dream 1970年的首张专辑，以电子冥想为名却实为实验性摇滚作品。评论指出当时乐队尚未使用合成器，主要以传统摇滚乐器制造声音实验，因此更应归入德国新兴的krautrock范畴，而非电子音乐范畴。专辑共有五首曲目，首曲Geburt（Genesis）中Schnitzler的刮擦式大提琴声占据主导地位。评论将作品与Pink Floyd的早期实验专辑A Saucerful Of Secrets和Ummagumma进行类比，认为其音乐风格介于前卫摇滚与自由即兴之间，并提及后续Ash Ra Tempel等德国实验团体的相似倾向。该专辑被视作乐队四个阶段中'粉红年代'的起点，也成为粉丝中评价两极化的争议之作，因为其风格与后来乐队成熟的电子路线差异较大。整体而言，这是一份带有历史梳理的详细乐评。

items.body: Review by arcane-beautiful — Morning Rituals by New Mexican Stargazers is a brilliant piece of ambient experimental music, that's very relaxing to listen to and overly melodic. The project is headed by multi instrumentalist Carter Eggert, who mixes live instrumentation and field noise with electronic loops. Written as 2 long pieces, it gives me a very Alan's Psychedelic Breakfast vibe, with ethereal loops that while on the long side, show off great composition skill. While it is a bit on the long side, it is reminiscent of a more electronic Mike Oldfield at times. I'd give this a low to mid 7 out of 10. The track I'd recommend is A.

items.body: Review by Chaoticreason — 4.5 stars.Superb tunes, Symphonic Prog Rock, whilst maintaining a very original sound.I am impressed by this album, their former album was good, but never quite reached the dizzying heights that this very addictive album manages to do. As you can see by the bands' genre designation (RIO/Avant-prog) this will not appeal to everyone. But! And, it is a huge BUT. This band has some real (dare I say it) catchy lines going on because they can write 'tunes'. The music is really not that far out. I would almost (though not quite) go as far as to say that this is 'progressive symphonic prog' in the sense that it is a genuine progression. The kind of symphonic prog that we all love, only from a slightly oblique angle. As much as we all wish that Genesis, Yes and ELP, etc had all written more great albums. They didn't. So here it is, the new pure sound of unadulterated Symphonic Progressive Rock.Here is an album that fully caries that torch of brilliance forward, into wholly new realms.This album has it, it is not bowing down to any former realms of music, it is a new creation. The way forward, the sound of now, pointing rockets at the sky. This is the future. This is Symphonic Progressive Rock.Miss this album at your own peril. I dare you to listen to it... and tell me that I am wrong.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑被定位为RIO/前卫摇滚与交响式进步摇滚的交汇点。评论者强调，尽管乐队带有前卫标签，但作品并未远离主流审美，仍保留了强烈的旋律性与可记忆的乐句，这在同类型乐队中较为少见。整体编曲将古典交响乐的厚重度与摇滚乐的冲击力结合，并在结构层面突破了传统进步摇滚的范式，加入了不规则的节奏变化与非常规的段落安排。评论者特别指出，这张专辑的成功在于将交响式进步的精髓推向新方向，既致敬了Genesis、Yes、ELP等经典乐队未能延续的音乐理想，又开辟了独立的听觉逻辑。弦乐、铜管与电声乐器之间的平衡据称是这张专辑的核心特征。

items.body: Review by Chaoticreason — 4.5 stars. I have a strange relationship with this band (then again, that is true of every band that I listen to). I generally put all my albums (some 2,500 or so, many more sit in the sidelines waiting for me to pick them up again, post removal from my playlist) on random play, so I frequently forget who the band is that I am playing. It ends up being a game of Russian roulette (no pun intended). Like hearing an album for the 1st time, except that you know the music, but can't remember the artist. I must confess to being blown away sometimes by a Roz Vitalis album that comes up randomly, and at other times thinking what the heck is this Rubbish. This is all of course down to how receptive my head is at that moment in time. All good music has its place in my playlist, but my head is not always up for some of the completely wild atonal stuff that is on my playlist. Whilst Roz Vitalis are certainly not in that category, of being for very specific moments, they have enough of an edge to sometimes make me love them and other times not want to play them. Whilst this may sound bad for my love of this band, that is quite simply not the case. Sometimes I love the Beatles, or some early Bob, but not all the time.So what do I make of this 25th anniversary record? Well, as it uses some of the highlight tracks from their vast opus, there are tracks on here that I do already know, but some of the arrangements have me guessing. I would say the band have played it fairly safe for long-term fans, it is a great idea to mix some old material with new sounds. I would also say, for sure, that this is a great introduction to a band that can push its sonic boundaries well beyond anything that they have done here. This is not to denigrate this record, I just feel that they wished to capture the more listenable side of their music, as opposed to alienating everybody with a full on expose of just how weird and wonderful their sound can be at times.Violinist, Vitaly Borodin certainly deserves mention, I only know his work with Vespero (another great Russian band), but will happily seek out the other bands he has played in (they being The Legendary Flower Punk & Vevil). He, as the rest of the band do, appear to have all had an obvious classically trained background. Still, the man sticks some really great solo work into this recording, that bares no real resemblance to what I think of as Classically trained violinist as doing. He plays an almost gypsy style (which I love) that overrides his classical training.So to sum this album up!Well, I would say that it is definitely a great gateway into their music, for those who have perhaps been put off in the past by their more oblique albums, (personally I love the more out there stuff. But! Only if I am in the mood). It is also great to hear some old tunes rearranged, especially with Vitaly Borodin on board, the band have really let him do his thing, as only he can do.This is definitely an album worth listening to if you have the slightest interest in music that pushes boundaries, but does not smash them to pieces, at least not here. (Totally free on Bandcamp as of writing this). This is a great place to start for such a diverse and original band. Not too much weirdness, but just enough for those sat on the fence to go for it. The recording quality makes it sound, at least, to my ears, as if it was recorded in a studio. Others may have a very different take on that thought, it is just my opinion.A great 25th anniversary recording.

items._cn_summary: 这是俄罗斯前卫摇滚乐队Roz Vitalis在2024年Garkundel音乐节现场录音的25周年纪念专辑。整张作品选取乐队历年曲目进行重新编排，在保留原有前卫摇滚骨架的同时注入了更易接受的现场演绎。小提琴手Vitaly Borodin是本张专辑的亮点之一，他以吉普赛式的即兴演奏手法超越了古典训练的框架，为作品增添了独特的东欧色彩与情感张力。整张唱片可被视为乐队作品的入门级入口，适合被其过往专辑中较为晦涩的实验元素劝退的听众，同时也为老乐迷提供了重新审视经典曲目的机会。

items.body: It comes back to control me What it said is stuck on me It comes from the shadows So elusive to me Portland duo Princess Ugly approach labour as something closer to possession on their new single, The Work, turning the ordinary language of obligation into a study of creation, anxiety, and control. J. Christopher-Rome’s lyrics begin with familiar pressures: unfinished tasks, the reluctance to ask for help, the nagging sense that something remains unresolved…before those pressures acquire a strange agency of their own. Work ceases to feel like an activity and begins behaving like a presence, capable of following its creator home. Christopher Moncrieffe builds that unease into the arrangement through clipped electronic rhythms, stern bass movement, and the mechanical forward motion of classic EBM. There is enough post-punk space around the instrumentation for Rome’s voice to carry the psychological weight, while the programming maintains a physical momentum suited equally to headphones and a crowded club. The tension comes from how naturally those two impulses coexist: the body is encouraged to move while the mind gets trapped inside a recurring thought. Rome delivers the words with the exhausted concentration of someone attempting to identify a fear while still living inside it. Memory becomes another form of labour, something requiring constant maintenance before it can be trusted, and even dreams appear subordinate to productivity. Images of dust, unfinished construction, and something sharp waiting in the dark give the song an almost metaphysical dimension. Creation rises out of debris, yet the resulting object seems capable of turning upon its maker. The song recognizes a contemporary condition in which occupation, identity, output, and self-worth have become increasingly difficult to separate. You build something, maintain it, remember why you started, and eventually discover that the structure has developed requirements of its own. Princess Ugly allows that cycle to remain unresolved, which suits a piece concerned with repetition and the unease of never reaching completion. Watch the video for The Work below: Listen to the Leæther Strip Remix of The Work below and order the single here. The Work (Leæther Strip Remix) by Princess Ugly Claus Larsen pushes those instincts toward the dance floor on the accompanying LEÆTHER STRIP Remix. His version thickens the percussion and sharpens the electro-industrial attack, giving the track a harder, more immediate propulsion without losing its underlying dread. Larsen treats the original’s anxiety as fuel, transforming psychological pressure into movement. Together, the two versions make The Work feel less like a conventional song about employment than an examination of creation becoming obligation, obligation becoming authority, and authority eventually learning how to follow you home. items._cn_summary: 这首单曲以"工作"为切入点，将日常义务的语言转化为对创作、焦虑与控制的探究。歌词从未完成的任务与不愿求助的微妙压力出发，逐步赋予工作以某种自主意识般的存在感，使其不再仅是行为，而成为跟随创作者回家的阴影。电子节奏被刻意切碎，贝斯线条冷峻，编曲在EBM的机械推进力与后朋克的空间感之间取得平衡，人声在器乐间隙中承载心理重量。Leæther Strip混音版本则将原曲的精神压力转化为舞池驱力，加厚打击层次，强化电工业的攻击性。整张作品关注的是职业、身份、产出与自我价值日益难以分离的当代境况，让创作的循环始终悬而未决。

items.body: It had been five years since the Spanish Dark-Electro project Asseptic Room released its previous album. Carlos Ruiz—formerly active as Dioxyde—and his companion Mario González now return with 16 new tracks that make up this fourth official album. Asseptic Room remains firmly rooted in dark, gloomy Electro, but this time the atmosphere takes center stage more than ever before. The songwriting is exceptionally detailed, yet the album’s greatest strength lies in the overwhelming sense of atmosphere it creates. At times, it even feels like the Soundtrack to a dark, dystopian film—Cinematic Dark-Electro would be a fitting description. The music is tormented and intense, driven by raw vocals delivered in both Spanish and English. Industrial elements occasionally emerge, adding extra power and texture to the already dark soundscape. Towards the end of the album, the music gradually becomes harder and more dancefloor-oriented. Personally, I still consider this to be the band’s strongest side, although that is, of course, a matter of taste. In any case, “Deconstructor” comes highly recommended for anyone with a passion for extremely Dark-Electro. The album may have flown somewhat under the radar, but it is certainly well worth discovering. (Rating:8). Listen to “Shame And Forgiveness”: Shame And Forgivness by Asseptic Room About Asseptic Room Asseptic Room is the Spanish dark electro project of Carlos Ruiz, who started as a DJ in Madrid in the late 1980s before forming Dioxyde with Marcos Calvo in 1998, releasing the debut album “Torschlusspanik”. Ruiz left Dioxyde in 2004 and founded Asseptic Room, releasing the albums “Morbid Visions” in 2006 and “Visceralofobia” in 2011 via Advoxya Records. Mario González joined the project, and the pair released the double album “Extinction Or Reawaken” via Advoxya Records. “Deconstructor” is Asseptic Room’s fourth official album, also released via Advoxya Records, arriving five years after its predecessor.

items._cn_summary: 西班牙暗潮电子项目 Asseptic Room 沉寂五年后带来第四张正式专辑，收录十六首新作。Carlos Ruiz 与 Mario González 在保留黑暗阴郁基调的同时，将氛围营造推向核心位置，乐句编排细节丰富，整体听感犹如一部反乌托邦电影的配乐。演唱部分使用西班牙语与英语交替，原始粗粝的人声与工业元素交织，强化了本就厚重的声场结构。专辑后半段逐步加重硬度与舞曲属性，向舞池取向过渡。双语歌词、电影化氛围以及工业质感的层次叠加，使作品在传统暗潮电子框架内呈现出更立体的叙事维度。Advoxya Records 作为独立厂牌提供发行支持，专辑虽传播范围有限，但其声音设计与氛围构建的用心程度值得暗潮与工业电子爱好者深入聆听。

items.body:
Key Chicago house architect Ron Trent departs the club for the bedroom under new alias La Marr, a new vent for his most romantic, sublime soundscapes, warmly advised FFO Detroit Escalator Company, Terre Thaemlitz, Wally Badarou, Klaus Schulze, MvO Trio

Light candles/incense and scatter petals for optimal effect when immersing in La Marr’s debut ‘Mood Programs’ EP, which finds a perfect home nestled amid Music From Memory’s precious, timeline-twining cuts of new age ambient, kosmiche, and Balearic wist. It’s also a natural, logical progression from the sort of depths usually secreted in Trent’s albums, but here given full sides to unfurl their functions, which we’re sure will also sound dead tasty, syrupy slow, on 33-not-45. 

He paints the lushest 12 min panorama of elliptical stereo pads, floating organ cloud structures and skin-stroke arps in ‘Good Magic’, edging on similar terrain to Terre Thaemlitz’s golden revision of Tangerine Dream’s ‘Love on a Real Train’, where a fine line of hand played drums emphasises the swaying groove - swooning either bed-ways or a little rug-cut, depending on your disposition - before ‘Clear’ hustles a palette of the slinkiest Afro-Latinate, Brazilian rhythms under big, dusky skies, hinting at Manuel Göttsching via MvO Trio. 

Your ears do not deceive you: this one is proper lush.

items._cn_summary: 芝加哥浩室建筑师Ron Trent以新别名La Marr发行首张EP《Mood Programs》，将创作重心从俱乐部转向卧室氛围场景。整张作品围绕立体声pad铺展，融合漂浮的管风琴音色层与手打鼓组律动，呈现十二分钟长的弧线式冥想结构。编曲中融入Afro-Latin与巴西节奏元素，与Manuel Göttsching式的序列循环及MvO Trio的质感形成对照。整体调性温暖而潮湿，强调长篇慢速展开而非舞池功能，适合33转黑胶低速聆听。作品延续了Trent专辑中常见的深层氛围探索，但在有限篇幅内为这些音色纹理提供了完整展开的空间，是其个人脉络中向更内向、更抒情境域的一次逻辑延伸。

Attending to an emergent TTT touchstone of... more
items.body:
TTT tack to classical chamber music with the intimately fuzzy recital of richly melodic works written between mid-14th and 21st centuries and performed by NYC’s Cop Tears, a trio of early and avant garde music specialists; Derek Baron, Cameron kapoor, and John Andrew Wilhite.

Attending to an emergent TTT touchstone of recent times - as in Jack Sheen’s works, thru aspects of Will Bankhead’s What We and Guild mixes - Cop Tears lean into interests in quieter chamber music laced with threads of lo-fi, folk and jazz that tie ‘The Rules of the Game’ to the label’s key corpus. The 13 pieces follow five years from the trio’s ‘Theodor Adorno: Piano Works’, and five again from their debut ‘Thirteen Harmonies (1986) Selections From John Cage’s ‘Apartment House 1776’’, with enchanting slants on cherry picked pieces that endure, some over 600 years later, on the strength of their timeless arrangements.

In key with the label's thing, everything is swaddled in ferric gauze - possibly posited on auld tape recorders - and holds a peculiar, homely, discordant charm (including fits of giggles and room noise) for the duration, which never tests the patience. The C.14th, polyphonic chanson Ars Nova masterpiece of Guillaume de Machaut ‘Puis qu’en oubli’ is the set’s oldest, along with ‘Quam pulchra est’, a mid-C.15th work for recorder trio by John Dunstable, placed on the same page with the more angular chamber jazz modernism of ‘Selections from Piano Sonata after a Conversation with Jonathan Gean (2016)’ and their take on the naïf wooze of ‘Children's Music, No. 1, II: Modern Dance (1973)’ by Valentin Silvestrov. Our percy is the dreamy, creaking baroque elegance of ’S’io men vo (1618)’, but it’s best advised to take it all in one at your leisure...
items._genre: contemporary classical / chamber music / lo-fi / folk / jazz
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是纽约三重奏Cop Tears对跨越六个多世纪音乐文献的一次重新诠释，选取从14世纪马肖的Ars Nova复调尚松到15世纪邓斯特布尔的录音器作品，再到Silvestrov及Cage相关作曲家的现代曲目，以早期音乐与先锋演奏者的双重身份进行演绎。所有作品被刻意裹上一层磁带般的朦胧质感，混入了低保真、民谣与爵士的微妙痕迹，呼应了该厂牌一贯的安静室内乐审美。录音保留了房间噪音与偶发的笑声，带有一种古怪的、不协和的家居式亲和力。整张专辑不追求学院派的精确，而是将古老旋律与当代演奏传统置于同一平面，强调编曲的永恒性而非时代风格的距离。13首作品构成一次跨度极大的聆听旅程，适合整张连续沉浸。

items.excerpt: Effortlessly easy on the ear and yet still somehow fathoms-deep, Tara Clerkin Trio’s latest is their most refined and fully-formed transmission yet, mining a precious sweetspot between chamber-jazz, Plone-style bric-a-brac electronics, Crescent’s lo-fi reveries and the urban pressure of the Young Echo collective, unpicking... more
items.body:
Effortlessly easy on the ear and yet still somehow fathoms-deep, Tara Clerkin Trio’s latest is their most refined and fully-formed transmission yet, mining a precious sweetspot between chamber-jazz, Plone-style bric-a-brac electronics, Crescent’s lo-fi reveries and the urban pressure of the Young Echo collective, unpicking decades of British musical history in the process. Trust, it’s a special one.

Like every great band, TCT know their history. They've grown up with and formed their identity in the shadow of Bristol's musical lore, whether it's The Pop Group, Massive Attack or Flying Saucer Attack, and when they use traceable elements, it feels like a believable part of their DNA. Thankfully, they meaningfully add to that narrative too, not adapting an aesthetic for easy consumption. Part of this might be down to their makeup; they formed in the late 20-teens from the ashes of the Tara Clerkin Band, a larger ensemble that Clerkin had put together to expand the scope of her folk-y pop compositions. And when most of the members moved on, stepbrothers Sunny-Joe Paradiso and Patrick Benjamin stuck around to see where the road might lead. All "proper" players, they've traditionally let their songs appear from what sounds like loose, casual improvisations, like you're tuned into Don Cherry's 'Organic Music Society' band running through Laika's 'Silver Apples of the Moon'.

So you get a song like the brilliant 'Ups & Downs', that simmers for a good four minutes with wheezing harmonium, double bass and clarinet, percussion just rumbling in the background somewhere, before a jerky sampled beat, Mellotron strings and Clerkin's voice would have you thinking Matt Elliott's behind the boards. But 'Somewhere Good' is also remarkably tight when it needs to be, walking a tightrope between easy breezy and meticulous with acrobatic skill. Opener 'Lake Walk', for example, sounds intentionally naive, jammed out loosely on synthesised and real woodwind that's caught in a vortex of Space Echo, before 'Lazy Daisy' cuts it short with its more ordered (but still kinda slouchy) beat-heavy dreampop atmosphere. It's where the album's shape really coagulates, between Broadcast's dramatic early EPs (back when they were touring with Plone) and Pram's best shit, just lightly tweezed at the edges, its creases relaxed to fit in with Laila Sakini's quietly genius 'Paloma'. And that mood carries the record even when Clerkin's voice - pursed into a soulful croon or a lackadaisical murmur - vanishes completely. One of the most gripping moments arrives with 'There Was a Nice Sunset', effortlessly matching slowcore drums with piano flourishes and synths, locking into the same general feeling but widening the boundaries, nodding to Adrian Sherwood's lysergic work on Creation Rebel's 'Starship Africa'. 

There's years of British musical history baked into this stuff, and yet it feels wholly new.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Tara Clerkin Trio迄今最成熟的作品，在室内爵士、Plone式的拼贴电子、Crescent的lo-fi梦幻与Bristol地下场景的都市张力之间找到了罕见的交汇点。乐队从民间流行三人组合Tara Clerkin Band的解散中重组而来，保留了stepbrothers Sunny-Joe Paradiso与Patrick Benjamin，延续了松散即兴的创作传统——听起来像是Don Cherry的Organic Music Society乐队在翻奏Laika的作品。专辑中手风琴、低音提琴、单簧管与采样鼓机、Mellotron弦乐交织，从《Ups & Downs》四分钟的缓慢酝酿到《Lake Walk》刻意制造的稚气合成器木管，再到《Lazy Daisy》中略带松垮的dream-pop节奏，呈现出松弛与精密之间的平衡。Clerkin的人声时而消失，仅留下《There Was a Nice Sunset》中慢核鼓机与钢琴、合成器的融合，向Adrian Sherwood为Creation Rebel制作的作品致意。数十年英国音乐史在这张唱片中被消化并转化，既有迹可循又全然新鲜。

items.body:
Konx-om-Pax plays to his love of Brum/Detroit/Berlin techno and bittersweet braindance on his label, Display Copy

Tom Scholefield’s project typically folds in aspects of his background as animator and graphic designer into the highly visual auditory synaesthetics of the ‘Naja Naja EP’. On the title tune he deftly unfolds monotone Brum techno and the steely drive of Claude Young or Mills bangers into a tearing chromatic rager, whereas ’Tarantula’ listens u a lot with its ribboning lead reminding of Clark on a garage-techno tip, and ‘Phantasmal’ spirals the arps to a bittersweet braindance pinnacle.
items._cn_summary: Konx-om-Pax（Tom Scholefield）的EP展现出鲜明的视觉化听觉美学，将动画师与平面设计师的背景融入声音设计。标题曲将伯明翰式单调Techno与底特律硬朗驱动的Techno相融合，演变为色彩撕裂的能量爆发；'Tarantula'采用车库Techno风格，丝带般展开的主音旋律令人联想到Clark；'Phantasmal'则将琶音盘旋至甜美与苦涩交织的braindance巅峰。整张作品在Brum/Detroit/Berlin三种Techno传统之间游走，兼有braindance的复杂层次感，发行于其个人厂牌Display Copy，具有独立地下气质。

items.body:
Habibi Funk continue to unveil Malay jazz to a broader audience with 2nd drop on new offshoot Audible Beauty Records, parsing choice morsels from Johari Salleh’s smooth jazz catalogue for Radio TV Malaysia...

“Habibi Funk’s new sister label Audible Beauty Records debut release: We originally came across Salleh's music after visiting Malaysia and Indonesia as part of some DJ gigs for Habibi Funk and were immediately head over heels with the music. A landmark collection retelling the untold story of Malaysian jazz featuring 9 songs from the legendary composer, arranger and trumpet player Johari Salleh. Salleh played a crucial role in shaping the sound of modern Malaysian music across radio, television, film and live performance and has composed dozens of popular songs in his decades long career. 

His personal musical passion always was jazz, reflected in this deep selection of jazz works that were previously unavailable unless you had one of the few dozen copies pressed locally in the 1970s. The album doesn’t only highlight his musical statue as a composer but also as a outstanding trumpet soloists bringing together jazz, spiritual undertones and Malaysian folkloric themes balancing slower pacing deep, modal grooves with more upbeat jazz funk leanings.

For fans of Salah Ragab, Ahmed Malek, Mulatu Astatke, Dollar Brand and co. The release includes extensive liner notes and previously unpublished archival photographs documenting Salleh’s career presented in a gatefold jacket with a 12 page booklet. Fully licensed from the Johari Salleh.”
items._genre: Malaysian jazz / modal jazz / jazz funk / folk jazz fusion
items._cn_summary: Habibi Funk旗下新厂牌Audible Beauty Records推出的第二张专辑，重新挖掘马来西亚作曲家、小号手Johari Salleh在1970年代为马来西亚广播电台录制的爵士乐作品。这些曲目此前仅以极少量本地压片形式存在，属于马来西亚现代音乐史上被忽视的篇章。专辑共收录九首作品，展现了Salleh作为作曲家和独奏小号手的双重身份，将爵士乐与灵性音乐元素、马来西亚民俗主题相融合，节奏编排上兼顾慢速深沉的调式律动与更为明快的爵士放克倾向。专辑附有详尽的厂牌解说词与未曾公开的档案照片，采用双折封面搭配十二页册装，从文化存档与音乐发掘两个维度呈现其价值。对于关注非洲与中东爵士复兴脉络的听众而言，这张来自东南亚的爵士考古构成了一条平行的听觉线索。

A Colourful Storm’s... more
items.body:
Selected and arranged by Jack Rollo and Elaine Tierney, Ballads’ is a waking-dream meander through beautiful, romantic, weird, exotic, intimate, un-categorisable music that shouldn't go together but yet somehow makes complete sense, offering a sort of spiritual life-enhancement in the process. 

A Colourful Storm’s Fleetway Tapes seems to has become the ideal place for skilled musical storytellers to flex their muscle, and on ‘Ballads’ the London-based duo turn their attention to the classic storytelling category of songcraft with the mix of forensic digging and poetic arrangement that has made their long-running NTS show a cult hit for many. Spanning a literate and cinematic world of sound with signature delicacy, they conjure a far flung and totally absorbing set whose track-listing remains impenetrable, and may well drive diggers to a tizzy. Suffice to say; numerous pearls lie within.

Sung in myriad tongues, the ballads range from the romantic and sentimental to the abstract and instrumental, spieling yarns that may not be fully understood, but with an atmosphere, pacing, and seductive vibe that's unmistakable.

For us, and so many, the mixtape of the decade.
items._genre: mixtape / ballad compilation / world music / experimental curation
items._cn_summary: 由Jack Rollo与Elaine Tierney精选并编排的《Ballads》是一张横跨国界与语种的歌谣合集，曲目以多种语言演唱，涵盖浪漫、抽象、器乐等多种情绪层次。A Colourous Storm的Fleetway Tapes厂牌持续聚焦富有叙事性的音乐挖掘，选曲跨越地域与类型，呈现出文学性与电影感兼具的声音脉络。整张合集以诗意的编排逻辑串联不同来源的曲目，气氛连贯而节奏从容，强调听觉氛围而非歌词理解。乐评将其誉为近十年最具代表性的mixtape式作品之一，体现出策展人独特的音乐视野与跨文化品味。

items.body:
A godfather of modern Malay jazz music is given his flowers by Habibi Funk’s new offshoot, Audible Beauty Records, pulling together smooth but vibrant archival gems on a tip shared with Salah Ragab, Ahmed Malek, Mulatu Astatke, Dollar Brand and co...

“Habibi Funk’s new sister label Audible Beauty Records debut release: We originally came across Soliao's music after visiting Malaysia and Indonesia as part of some DJ gigs for Habibi Funk and were immediately head over heels with the music.

A landmark collection retelling the untold story of Malaysian jazz featuring 11 songs from the legendary composer, arranger and pianist Alfonso Soliano, originally recorded for Radio Television Malaysia (RTM) and only released in a run of a few dozen copies for radio broadcast. Widely regarded as one of the foundational figures of Malaysian music, Soliano blended jazz, Latin influences and traditional Malay musical forms into a uniquely local sound of all original compositions. The recordings also feature contributions from some of Malaysia’s most important musicians and composers of the era, including Johari Salleh and Ahmad Nawab. 

For fans of Salah Ragab, Ahmed Malek, Mulatu Astatke, Dollar Brand and co. The release includes extensive liner notes and previously unpublished archival photographs documenting Soliano’s life and legacy. Includes a special gatefold LP with a 12-page booklet attached to the sleeve and featuring in-depth essays, archival photography and historical material. Fully licensed from the Soliano family.”
items._genre: Malaysian jazz / Latin jazz / world fusion / archival
items._cn_summary: Habibi Funk旗下新厂牌Audible Beauty Records的首发作品，聚焦马来西亚爵士乐先驱Alfonso Soliano的档案录音。收录11首原本仅供马来西亚广播电视（RTM）播出、仅以极少量拷贝发行的原创曲目，融合爵士、拉丁元素与马来传统音乐形式，形成独具地方特色的声音。这些录音还汇集了Johari Salleh、Ahmad Nawab等马来西亚重要音乐人的贡献。发行版本采用gatefold双折LP设计，附有12页小册子，包含详细论文、档案照片及历史资料，全面记录Soliano的音乐生涯与遗产。作为东南亚爵士历史的重新挖掘，与Salah Ragab、Ahmed Malek、Mulatu Astatke、Dollar Brand等非洲及中东爵士先驱形成跨文化对话，对世界音乐与爵士交叉领域的听众具有特殊价值。

items.body: This music tells of the passage of time, with sparse humorous and facetious tones punctuating the moodier ensemble. Each track is elaborated and designed as a subtle, sentient vignette in the mind of a daydreaming smoker and ordinary thinker who opens his soul and invites the listener to witness his hope, fear, despair, and intricate yet playful reflections. A slow journey through existential wandering 20 Cigarettes by Jesper Møller Nielsen   French indie net label with a substantial production, navigating from lo-fi electronics and leftfield minimalism to noisy soundscapes and atmospheric alt-pop, Lotophagus Records offers here a new album by guitarist and sound explorer Jesper Moller Nielsen. The compositions are based on the spoken words and personal diary of multidirectional intermedia artist Jordane Prestrot, known for his essentially narrative-focused experimental works, often using poetry and irony as their main ingredients. The album evolves as a slow journey through existential wandering, anecdotal and reflective situations. Each smoked cigarette represents a distinct personal life moment, suggesting a state of mind and various encounters with oneself. The minimal, deliberately rough-hewn guitar patterns are articulated around thoughts translated through spoken words, while various sonic explorations, effects, and processed field recordings enhance the album’s narrative purpose. This music tells of the passage of time, with sparse humorous and facetious tones punctuating the moodier ensemble. Each track is elaborated and designed as a subtle, sentient vignette in the mind of a daydreaming smoker and ordinary thinker who opens his soul and invites the listener to witness his hope, fear, despair, and intricate yet playful reflections. There is something in this album that evokes the literary wanderings and explorations of consciousness found in Italo Svevo. In itself, the music and its fragmented, bluesy melodies in slow motion suggest feelings akin to those found in road movies, notably the films of Jim Jarmusch. 20 Cigarettes is recommended for fans of desolate guitar microsounds, field recordings, and evocative, semi-improvised ambiences in the spirit of Loren Connors & David Grubbs, Western Grey, Luca Nasciuti, and Sqürl. 20 Cigarettes is available on Lotophagus. [Bandcamp] 20 Cigarettes by Jesper Møller NielsenThe post Jesper Møller Nielsen :: 20 Cigarettes (Lotophagus) first appeared on Igloo Magazine.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以二十支香烟为隐喻，构建了一段缓慢穿梭于存在主义漫游的旅程。核心创作基于Jordane Prestrot的日记体独白文字，吉他手与声音探险者Jesper Møller Nielsen以刻意粗糙的简约吉他线条为骨架，融入田野录音、效果处理与多种声音探索手段，强化叙事氛围。每支香烟对应一个独特的人生瞬间，承载希望、恐惧、绝望与戏谑反思，情绪在忧郁中点缀幽默与讽刺。专辑呈现出碎片化的布鲁斯旋律，类似于公路电影中的沉思时刻，尤其让人联想到Jim Jarmusch作品的影像质感。作为法国独立厂牌Lotophagus的出品，专辑融合了低保真电子、左翼极简主义与氛围另类流行，推荐给偏好荒凉吉他微型声响、田野录音及半即兴氛围的听众，与Loren Connors、David Grubbs等人的美学一脉相承。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — With Phil Miller, Pip Pyle, Amanda Parsons, Jimmy Hastings, and the very architect of the Canterbury scene, Dave Stewart, all members of Hatfield and the North, National Health was formed, joined by bassist Neil Murray, who came from Colosseum II and would also work with Bill Bruford during the rehearsals for Feels Good to Me.Right from the start with "Tenemos Roads," there is a distinct energy, stemming from a rhythm section (drums and bass) that leans toward aggressive jazz-rock fusi�n, to which Jimmy Hastings' bass clarinet adds a supernatural, postmodern air, further enhanced by Dave Stewart's keyboards. The jazz-rock turns psychedelic while incorporating a funky groove that keeps things fresh; then Amanda Parsons enters, singing atonally, sounding forever ethereal, like the soundtrack to a gateway into another dimension. Her style differs from how Annette Peacock might sound with Bill Bruford's band, yet she also possesses a quality reminiscent of Sally Oldfield.The music supports her, and subsequently, she supports the music, through both the up-tempo passages and the moments where the action pauses and both the guitar and her voice explore high registers. The composition elevates the piece beyond any single genre. That sense of confusi�n, and the intent of social critique during a turbulent era, also translates into the music and forms an integral part of it.Frank Zappa's One Size Fits All is another essential reference, as are all the bands Stewart was involved with, from Arzachel and Egg, with their classical influences, to the power of Khan alongside Steve Hillage. "Brujo" reveals another facet of the band, featuring Amanda Parsons channeling Annie Haslam; the action is driven simultaneously by her vocals, bass, and keyboards, before shifting into jazz-style improvisation. This album is packed with music, and it shows, as fleeting piano passages give way to keyboards played at breakneck speed that never cease to offer up new melodies, delivering the best of a live concert experience within a studio setting.One could say that the jazz-rock style of "Borogoves" is certainly obscure and intricate, perhaps akin to Brand X, yet Dave Stewart plays the clavinet there, bringing back a funky feel, while Phil Miller's distorted guitar seems to weave through the spaces left open for it. However, its follow-up, "Borogoves, Part One", moves away from those cited references; once again, it is the composition itself that lends the piece its distinctive character and individuality. There is a martial, existentialist quality to the music, heightened, of course, by Amanda Parsons' vocals.Following an initial cacophony of keyboards, "Elephants" serves as a showcase for Phil Miller, before Dave Stewart alternates with his own prowess on acoustic and electric piano, joined by Nick Levitt's synthesizers, delivering fusion riffs that would not only set a precedent but define an era. Jazz-rock had never come so close to being orchestral and symphonic, at least not within the sonic framework established by National Health on their debut, which was rooted in the Canterbury compositional style.
items._cn_summary: 这张1978年的专辑汇集了Hatfield and the North多位核心成员，包括吉他手Phil Miller、键盘手Dave Stewart及鼓手Pip Pyle，并加入了Colosseum II出身的贝斯手Neil Murray。乐评重点描述了各曲目的音乐特征：开场曲以激进的爵士摇滚节奏为基础，搭配Jimmy Hastings的低音单簧管与Stewart的键盘营造超自然氛围；女声Amanda Parsons的无调性演唱贯穿全篇，被比作Annie Haslam与Sally Oldfield的结合体。专辑在爵士摇滚框架内融入了迷幻、放克与即兴元素，Stewart的键盘与Miller的吉他在不同曲目中交替主导，从快速跑动的键盘独奏到失真吉他的穿插，展现出强烈的作曲意识与现场感。整体上，乐评将这张作品定位为Canterbury场景的延伸，融合了Zappa式的社会批判性与复杂编曲。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — There are many versions of Soft Machine, but only one Allan Holdsworth. There is the Soft Machine of Kevin Ayers, the one with Robert Wyatt, the era featuring Mike Ratledge and Elton Dean, and the later period with Karl Jenkins. Yet Holdsworth brought his signature sound to groups like Tony Williams' Lifetime and Nucleus, as well as later projects such as U.K. and Bill Bruford's solo band. Which brings us to Bundles, where he would also share the bill with bassist Roy Babbington, with whom he had worked on the 1972 Nucleus album Belladonna.While the style of fusion they were developing was already becoming increasingly electrified, Holdsworth's arrival brought powerful riffs that, combined with Mike Ratledge's synthesizers and organ, shaped the main suite, "Hazard Profile." The guitar scales are underpinned by Roy Babbington's tireless bass and Rhodes piano notes that drift like butterflies against the sky of 1975; the truly transcendent moment is the ensuing sequence, aided by the organ, which turns Holdsworth's notes like the pages of a book, gathering layer upon layer of information. One page features virtuosic guitar work that invites us to follow along; another presents piano and acoustic guitar in the suite's second part, capturing the poetic spirit of the era; the fourth section is more intense, almost reminiscent of Cream, save for the syncopated drum rhythm driving the tempo, setting the stage to accelerate into the fifth and final movement, where Karl Jenkins enters on the saxophone.After "Gone Sailing", a track with echoes of Ralph Towner, "Bundles" resumes the initial quest; the guitar navigates curves and corners, venturing into every nook and cranny with clockwork precisi�n, where the drum cymbals act as alarms and the bass serves as the second hand, tirelessly marking the relentless passage of time. The momentum never falters, not even for Holdsworth as "Land of the Bag Snake" begins, since the tracks are seamlessly linked, much like the flowers and privet hedge on the album cover, forming a unified whole where butterflies take flight; "The Man Who Waved at Trains" then continues the journey, albeit at a slower, steady, jazz-infused pace.Karl Jenkins and his oboe provided the missing touch, casting a spell over that timeless afternoon, an afternoon of backyards, plants, and sunshine. Much like on the debut album, the tracks unfold like pages turned by the wind, one after another; amidst this rhythm, Peff enters with keyboards and saxophone, conjuring a dreamlike, otherworldly atmosphere. Where did the violence go? Where did this calm, reminiscent of an endless siesta, come from? It returns through those same instruments, though momentarily clouded by the all-consuming, eternal keyboard. Mike Ratledge and Karl Jenkins vie for the spotlight in the finale, a tour de force where neither truly wins, for the real victor is Soft Machine. "The Floating World" serves as a sort of electronic elegy, a chance to catch one's breath after a relentless journey, an experience that was far from wasted, however, for it undoubtedly leaves the spirit feeling truly fulfilled.
items._cn_summary: 这张1975年的专辑将软机器的坎特伯雷派前卫爵士摇滚推向电气化融合的新阶段。全恩·霍尔斯沃斯的加入带来了强力和弦与炫技式吉他独奏，与迈克·拉特利奇的合成器、管风琴以及罗伊·巴宾顿的低音线和罗德钢琴形成复杂对话。主打组曲《Hazard Profile》以多乐章结构展开，从吉他主导的密集段落过渡到钢琴与原声吉他的抒情段落，最终以卡尔·詹金斯的萨克斯收尾。专辑中后段的《The Man Who Waved at Trains》以双簧管营造出梦幻氛围，键盘与萨克斯在终曲中相互竞奏。整体编曲精密，乐器层次丰富，呈现出统一而流动的整体感。

items.body: I’m taking a ride with my best friend’s girlfriend, and she used to be mine. Love crime. Detroit duo Credit Card make music for the hour when the club floor has acquired the adhesive properties of flypaper, the strobe has erased everyone’s face, and somebody in a leather jacket is conducting a one-sided argument with a subwoofer. Their new single, Love Crime, finds Shaun Hunter handling vocals, synth, and noise while Max Dameron supplies programming, synth, and guitar. Together, they turn romantic misconduct into a hard, queasy sprint through downtown. Love Crime is the second single from Credit Card’s forthcoming debut album, Devil’s Night / Dead Internet, due August 14, 2026. The title suggests either a municipal emergency or the browser history of a recently divorced nightclub promoter, which is more or less the territory the duo occupies. Their synth punk is aggressive, distorted, and built for physical response, though the song’s real pressure comes from the dawning suspicion that desire has selected the worst available route and locked the doors, and nobody involved appears eager to slow down. The sludginess of their sound brings to mind Nine Inch Nails as well as the Soft Moon – it is hypnotic in is raw power. The setup is luridly simple. A man takes a nighttime drive with his best friend’s girlfriend, who also happens to be his former lover. Betrayal, jealousy, and old possession rights crowd into the back seat, where nobody has remembered to fasten a seat belt. The ride carries the thrill of stolen intimacy, yet every beat pushes the characters closer to the embarrassing conclusion that wanting someone can be less a grand passion than a very efficient method of ruining several friendships at once. Hunter delivers the vocal with a cold, accusatory focus, sounding equally implicated and appalled. Dameron’s programming presses forward in blunt mechanical surges, while the synths bend around the rhythm with sinister, sinuous purpose. Guitar and noise roughen the edges without smothering the hook. The result feels immediate and dangerous, like overhearing a confession through the bathroom wall and realizing the names are familiar. On Love Crime, Credit Card makes bad judgment sound fast, stylish, and briefly irresistible. The song understands that romance often provides its own getaway vehicle, though it remains notably unreliable when the police lights appear in the mirror. Listen to Love Crime below and order the single here. Devil’s Night / Dead Internet by CREDIT CARDCredit Card has been building considerable attention in Detroit through shows governed by strobe lights, mosh pits, leather jackets, and beats capable of troubling nearby foundations. Their first seven-inch single, “(CC)” (a Germs reference) sold out at its release show, leaving the group with the enviable problem of having insufficient merchandise and an increasingly attentive audience. Credit Card is readying their debut “mixtape” for a Summer 2026 release, and local crowds in Detroit already sound eager to be flattened by it. items.body: Within progressive music, and especially within its odd sister-genre zeuhl, there are many competing forces. This makes sense, of course: a genre known for musical experimentation must, by force, include contradiction because that's how our brains often perceive complexity. Especially in music, where the competing forces of harmony and dissonance make up so much of our perception. Specifically in progressive rock, we can identify a few central tensions: melody, dissonance, tightness, expansiveness, and more. Papangu first burst into our perception with Holoceno, an album that was a sort of conflagration created from all of these tensions being driven to their brink. They followed that up with Lampião Rei, which was journey down one path, namely one of "open", "thin", and expansiveness sounds. Now, the Brazilian ensemble returns with another version, this time reaching deep into the core of progressive rock and bringing back one of its most defining attributes: brightness.Where Holoceno was tight like a ball of magma and Lampião Rei was rarified like a cloud, Celestial takes after its namesake and shines like the sun or the stars. First and foremost in creating this brightness are the synths. Instead of the all encompassing and redolent sound of Holoceno, Celestial is characterized with a sweet, warm, and fantastical synth sound which immediately sets the stage for exploration. Fans of progressive rock will immediately reach for the Yes comparison but there is more here than simple homage; Papangu are proving themselves masters of this sound as well, creating truly engrossing and captivating passages with the synths. My favorites are on "Colosso", the second track, an agile, light-hearted, and transportive affair that works wonders on the heart.It also has great usage of my second favorite on this album: bass. Papangu have chosen a "natural" and rich tone to couple with the synths here and "Colosso" has some of the best "conversations" between synth and bass that I've heard. Of course the guitars and the drums play a major role in these discussions; the drums are especially important for this track, and for the album. But there is something so joyous in how the bass and synths work here, something in their agility and subtilty that communicates the main accent or theme of the album. "Celeste", further down the album, is another magnificent example of this collaboration and probably my favorite track on the album in its whirling, jittery pace.In a way, this lighter tone serves to make Celestial feel more approachable and less intricate but this, of course, is a mistake. With a ten-part concept at its core, and multiple genres swimming within its embrace, Celestial has a lot of intricacy to it. In a way, it is less accessible because it is also less upfront with its ambition. It requires that the listener commit fully to its journey, a staple of the sort of progressive rock being referenced here. Luckily, this is quite easy to do as the album reveals more and more of its beauty on repeated listens. We haven't covered even a fragment of what's waiting for you on Celestial, from mysterious vocals, through breakneck grooves and folks sensibilities, and all the way to fusion rock and psychedelic crescendos. If you clicked on this review, you probably already knew I was only going to be able to capture a slight part of one of progressive rock's most intricate bands and you were right. Papangu have once more released a work of music on their own terms, completely dedicated to their craft and its execution. Its a different path up the mountain but oh boy, is the view just as gorgeous, awash in the rays of a bright, warm sun promising many valleys and peaks before the journey is done. Step forwards, won't you? Celestial by Papangu Celestial will be released on August 7th. You can, and should, click through to the Bandcamp link above to pre-order it.
items._cn_summary: 巴西部队Papangu的第三张专辑延续了Zeuhl与前卫摇滚的血脉，以合成器为主导音色，营造出温暖明亮、富有幻想色彩的听感。贝斯与合成器之间的对话是专辑核心亮点，《Colosso》轻盈灵动，展现出敏捷的器乐互动；《Celeste》节奏旋转跳跃，被视为专辑最佳曲目。虽然表面音色趋于明亮易接近，专辑内核实则包含十段式概念结构和多重风格交汇的复杂性，要求听众全情投入。鼓与吉他在编曲讨论中同样承担重要角色，共同构建出富有层次的前卫声响空间。整体而言，这是一张在传统前卫摇滚张力结构内进行精致探索的作品。
