items.body: La Division Technique, the French electronics project of Philippe Saintlos, releases “L’inversion des pôles” with Pascal Comelade as a limited, numbered 7″ vinyl edition of 200 copies through Ubahn. The record is out now. L’inversion des pôles by La Division Technique avec Pascal Comelade La Division Technique and Comelade press two tracks to a numbered 7 inch “L’inversion des pôles” holds two tracks, “Anaphores” on the A side and “Syncopes” on the B side, both composed by Comelade and Saintlos. Comelade plays grand piano, vertical piano, Farfisa organ, an Emenee plastic guitar and a Roland RD 300 SX keyboard, with “Syncopes” adding an EMS-AKS synthesizer and a Koma Elektronik FT201. Saintlos contributes a Korg MS10, an Arturia MiniBrute, a Nord Lead X2, a Yamaha RX11 drum machine, an ARP Odyssey and a Poly D clone Minimoog. The two recorded the pair of tracks with Raph Dumas between November 2024 and April 2026; Dumas also mastered the release, and Saintlos produced it and designed the sleeve. Each of the 200 copies is individually numbered. About La Division Technique La Division Technique is an electronics project from France, founded and directed by Philippe Saintlos, built around old-school electronics, dark soundscapes, minimal synths and industrial-ambient textures played on analog synthesizers, filters, guitars, voices and spatial sound recordings. A 2017 meeting with the label Rotorelief led to the release of the album “Unexpected Works, Random Systems,” drawn from tape recordings dating to the 1980s. A second album, “Nebula,” followed in 2019 on Rotorelief and Ubahn. The project returned in 2023 with “Traversant les cités liquides,” and issued “Tristes Machines,” its fourth album, on Ubahn in 2025, alongside the 2024 single “A Beginners Guide to Brian Eno…Baby’s On Fire.” Saintlos has also co-founded the labels Ditec, Semantic and Odessa. Pascal Comelade, born in Montpellier in 1955, is a self-taught French Catalan musician who debuted with the electronic-leaning album “Fluences,” influenced by Heldon, before building a body of work centered on toy instruments played through his Bel Canto Orquestra; he has recorded with Robert Wyatt, Faust, Christophe Miossec and P.J. Harvey among others. His work with La Division Technique on “L’inversion des pôles” pairs his toy-instrument and acoustic keyboard playing with Saintlos’s analog synthesizer sound.

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body: Review by Abrasmatheus — Coming to this album, I expected something much closer to the band's later soft rock sound. Like many listeners, I first knew Ambrosia through songs such as "Biggest Part of Me," so discovering their self-titled debut was quite a surprise. Rather than polished adult contemporary, this record presents a fascinating blend of melodic soft rock and progressive rock, creating an identity that feels both sophisticated and accessible. It easily exceeded my expectations.One of the album's greatest strengths is the balance between memorable melodies and progressive arrangements. While the music rarely reaches the complexity of the major symphonic prog bands of the era, it incorporates shifting structures, rich keyboard textures, dynamic contrasts, and tasteful instrumental passages without sacrificing accessibility. The result is an album that can appeal both to progressive rock fans and to listeners who enjoy melodic rock from the 1970s.The opening track, "Nice, Nice, Very Nice," immediately establishes this identity. Its polished production, layered vocals, and elegant keyboard work remind me at times of the atmosphere later associated with The Alan Parsons Project, while still maintaining Ambrosia's own personality. It is an excellent introduction and one of the reasons the album makes such a strong first impression.My favorite tracks are "Time Waits for No One," "Holdin' on to Yesterday," and especially "Make Us All Aware." The latter stands out for its stronger progressive character, interesting rhythmic development, and satisfying structural variations. Another highlight is "Mama Frog," whose instrumental approach occasionally brings to mind the energy of Emerson, Lake & Palmer and even some of King Crimson's more adventurous moments. The closing epic, "Drink of Water," is another outstanding composition, giving me the feeling of hearing Crosby, Stills & Nash interpreted through a progressive rock lens. It is a beautiful and memorable conclusion to the album.Instrumentally, the album is consistently enjoyable. The keyboards and synthesizers play a central role, adding color and atmosphere throughout the record, while the vocals remain expressive without becoming overdramatic. The musicianship is polished, serving the songs rather than existing simply to demonstrate technical ability.Although the album incorporates obvious soft rock influences, I still consider it a genuinely progressive rock release. The frequent changes in mood, carefully crafted arrangements, extended compositions, and willingness to experiment separate it from conventional soft rock albums of the period. At the same time, it avoids excessive complexity, jazz-oriented improvisation, or the grand symphonic approach that characterized many of its contemporaries. That accessibility is one of its greatest strengths rather than a weakness.Lyrically, I did not focus closely on the individual songs, but they complement the reflective and uplifting atmosphere created by the music. Combined with the warm production and melodic songwriting, the album maintains a consistently pleasant listening experience from beginning to end.Perhaps the greatest compliment I can give this album is that I never find myself wanting to skip a track. There are no weak moments here, and each song contributes something meaningful to the overall flow. The atmosphere is inviting, melodic, and subtly adventurous, making it an album I continue returning to years after first discovering it.I would recommend this record to anyone who enjoys the intersection of progressive rock and 1970s soft rock. Listeners who demand highly technical, symphonic, or heavy progressive music may find it too restrained, but those looking for sophisticated songwriting with progressive touches should find plenty to appreciate.

items._cn_summary: 这张1975年的同名专辑展现了旋律摇滚与前卫摇滚的融合，键盘与合成器在编曲中占据核心位置，营造出层次丰富的声场。曲目在保持可听性的同时引入了结构变化与节奏发展，'Make Us All Aware'和'Mama Frog'等作品带有较强的前卫色彩，后者偶尔闪现出ELP与King Crimson式的器乐能量。终曲'Drink of Water'将CSNY式的和声美学置于前卫框架内，形成绵长而内省的收尾。整体制作精良，乐器服务于歌曲结构，技术展示克制。不过从用户偏好的实验、前卫、爵士、即兴等角度来看，这张作品仍属70年代主流摇滚范畴，缺乏真正的实验性突破或跨类型融合，与当代前卫、爵士、电子等领域的距离较远。

items.body: Review by UMUR — "Undeceived" is the second full-length studio album by Norwegian metal act Extol. The album wasreleased through Endtime Productions in June 2000. It�s the successor to "Burial" from December 1998although the two full-length album releases are bridged by the November 1999 "Mesmerized" EP. Therehas been no lineup changes since "Burial", so it�s the same quintet lineup who recorded "Burial",who also recorded "Undeceived".Stylistically Extol have developed upon the hard-to-define extreme metal style of their debut albumand Undeceived is another interesting hybrid death/black/progressive metal release from the band.The Christian themed lyrics are still in place but Extol for the most part keep their lyrics incheck and make sure they are not preachy/praise God type Christian themed lyrics. These lyrics dealmore with mental struggles, temptations, and how to overcome various issues in your life (by findingthe light/Jesus/God). The first thing you notice when listening to "Undeceived" is how well playing Extol are. These guysperform their music with great skill and conviction and both the harsh and the clean vocals whichare present in the music are also well performed. The sound production values are also on a highlevel, providing the material with the best possible platform to shine. The songwriting is variedand challenging but maybe lacks a bit in the immediate catchiness department. The more you listenthe more you remember the songs, but it�s not an album featuring big hooks. Upon conclusion Extol are arguably an intriguing band and "Undeceived" is a good quality releasefrom them, but their songwriting could prosper from a more concise formula. We always praise band�sfor being progressive and incorporating a lot of sections and different time signatures, but to myears Extol is a band who are best when they play their most simple and atmospheric parts. That�swhen their music has most impact. A 3.5 star (70%) rating is deserved.(Originally posted on Metal Music Archives).

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是挪威乐队Extol的第二张全长录音室作品，延续了首张专辑难以归类的极端金属风格，将死亡金属、黑金属与前卫金属融为一体。歌词以基督教为主题，但并非直白的赞美诗式表达，更多关注内心挣扎、诱惑与如何克服生命中的困境（通过寻找信仰之光）。音乐演奏技术与信念感俱佳，清嗓与极端人声并用，制作水准精良。作曲丰富多变且具挑战性，但在即时抓耳方面稍有欠缺，需要反复聆听才能记住旋律。乐评认为乐队在简洁、氛围化的段落中表现最佳，复杂的结构与多变的拍号反而削弱了音乐的冲击力。整体而言，这是一张品质不错的作品，但作曲若能更精炼将更上一层楼。

items.body:
Amsterdam duo Kamma & Masalo play to deep house’s frothier ends on a maiden 12” on personal label Brighter Days, named after their rangy ’23 compilation for Rush Hour.

The OG ‘Can’t Fake the Feeling’ shakes up a proper, fruity handbag groove lit with whooshy fireworks and sounding like the soundtrack to some dodgy Retro promo, also found nipped and tucked for radio mix. The K&M Unity Dub is miles better, flexing some Factory style circuit muscle with haughty wiggle and lean beefcake mince.
items._cn_summary: 阿姆斯特丹二人组Kamma & Masalo在自家厂牌Brighter Days发行的首张12寸黑胶，延续了他们此前在Rush Hour合辑中的方向。标题曲带有水果味的手提包律动与烟火音效，电台混音版本对此做了精简。而K&M Unity Dub更为出色，展现了Factory厂牌式的电路肌理，傲慢的摇摆感与精简有力的节奏线条相结合。整张作品定位于deep house较为轻快的面向，融合disco元素与俱乐部舞曲美学，制作精致但并未走向实验或前卫的边界，更偏向舞池实用主义而非声音探索。

items.body: As Henry Rollins and Ian MacKaye open up The Cramps’ vaults for a sonic overhaul and a consolidation of the band’s business affairs, Julian Marszalek takes a deep dive into their back catalogue to offer 10 points of entry for novices and converts alike. Portrait by David Godlis It’s strange to think that it’s now been two decades since The Cramps last visited this side of the Atlantic and 17 years since singer Lux Interior’s untimely passing, thus bringing the band’s long and storied saga to an end. And yet in the 21st century they have remained one of those rare bands whose influence continues to spread like mould on discarded garbage with the likes of Jack White, The Limiñanas, Spiritualized... The post The Strange World Of… The Cramps appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评聚焦于The Cramps的精选合辑，由Henry Rollins与Ian MacKaye主导重新整理乐队曲库资产。文章梳理了乐队跨越数十年的音乐遗产，提及Lux Interior离世已17年，但其影响力仍在Jack White、Spiritualized等后辈乐队中延续。乐评为新手和乐迷提供了10个切入点来探索乐队庞大的唱片目录。The Cramps的音乐根植于psychobilly与rockabilly传统，融合朋克与车库摇滚的粗粝质感，将B级片美学与原始摇滚能量结合。文中提到David Godlis为其拍摄的肖像照，为这篇回顾增添了视觉史料价值。作为一篇导引式乐评，它更多是目录性质的整理而非深度音乐分析，对熟悉该乐队的老乐迷而言信息增量有限。

items.body: Review by Steve Conrad — And The Light is shining in the darkness, and the darkness did not overtake it.SLUG COMPARISON"Slug Comparison is the solo project of Canadian artist Doug Harrison, primarily known as the vocalist for progressive rock/metal band, Fen."- from the artist's bio.Credits:Doug Harrison: vocals, guitar, bass, programmingRandall Stoll: drumsAll songs written and produced by Doug Harrison.And may I say, here are some impressions of this impeccable EP: Somber. Thoughtful. Melancholy. Dark, with faint traces of light. Moody. Rich with meaning and texture and depth. Music and lyrics germane, inextricable, worth pondering. Not a note or chord or lyric or vocal line misplaced or overplayed or unnecessary. Evocative."Cold In Cold Out""Cold in cold out/ that's how it goes/ in with a cry/ and out with a moan"?This EP has six tracks playing for a total time of twenty-six minutes, forty-two seconds.Yet in the best possible way, it seems much longer, and much shorter than that."Much longer", because there is so much packed into each song, so much emotion, so much to ponder, so much complexity even while on the surface seeming so simple, so much heart and soul and mind and body."Much shorter", because when the listener gets into the flow, discovers the moods and rhythms and sensibilities of each song- it seems over almost before it began.Consider the title itself, "Cold In Cold Out". Frankly, I don't get the sense that Doug Harrison commits to paper, then to tape, then on to the next iterations of music, anything that is extraneous or throw-away or superfluous.What- You Thought I Would Explain it All?All right- since you're paying me good money to write this review (well, then again, maybe not)- I think this EP is a meditation on death, heartache, birth, betrayal?and some faint signs of hope, wrapped within beguiling, sonorous, melodic music, and helmed by the wistful, powerful, emotive, tender voice of Harrison telling his truths.For me, birth and death can be cold things- the baby abruptly expelled into the buzzing, blooming world from her nourishing, safe womb. And, the brave soul who feels the breath of the reaper coming ever closer, who finds the tongue of the hollow seeking to suck the life force from the increasingly vulnerable husk.Look again and think about the album art pictured above: the enormous full moon, the umbilical cord/root system trailing toward the fallen traveler, the spectral hills, the blooming night flowers and ferns, the clouds with silver linings.And the opening track, "Tongue of the Hollow"- who is singing to us of dying (and being evocative, how is it that this instantly makes me recall my mother's dying- her reaching for things only she could see in the air, her slowly wasting away yet her life-breaths which she did not wish to relinquish)? Why is it that I recalled my sister and I needing to make decisions about mother's few remaining things, even before she died- and feeling like some kind of heartless parasite removing them one by one?Who is "the stranger above whose footsteps creak in beautiful time"?And all of it set in this solemn, somber tune, austere classical guitar, simple but powerful drumming, building, growing?"oh when the melody pours its wine/ out of the body, out of the mind", and the stranger stepping once more "to beautiful song"."To Whom Would You Answer"My point is, when I raise the question of "the voice" within the lyrics, about who is saying these things, to whom, and in what context, I'm saying that these, in concert with the way the song is constructed, create a tiny "universe" that requires thought, attention, and care- all of which I find refreshing and challenging!I "hear" Doug Harrison's music as an intensely absorbing example of these qualities. Musically, in "To Whom Would You Answer", we hear the hushed, restrained voice issuing languid menace to the unidentified recipient, who is being threatened with humiliation and perhaps liquidation. The wah-guitar tones suggest the ambiguity of the piece. The gritty bass and pulsing drums in verse two highlight how Harrison uses tonal shift in subtle or obvious ways to drive the music and the message. The octave vocals later also create menace and melancholy- Harrison clearly thinks through every aspect and every line- and I wonder, as an old musician, how crazy he drives himself trying to get things "right".And to whom WILL you answer, especially if these self-same accusers paradoxically lionize you? Hang your face on the wall?"Back to the World"A few noteworthy things about this track- it starts with a much lighter touch, and the listener is nearly relieved that the ominous and dark tones of the album might be mitigated with some light and hope. We hear a lighter guitar line, clean chords, melodic voice, clear guitar lead.HOWEVER (listen up to the lyrics, dang it) the protagonist seems to be encountering a past love and finding a mix of gladness at seeing her again, and shame for earlier not being there for her: "good seeing you out again/ on a day I thought was ruined", and then, "I never did one drop for you/ just outta my hands ignored you" and, "you fought black wind on a ledge/ I dropped my eyes/ and hung my head".And this exquisite line, "you've come back to the world/ when I'm all but missing from my life?and I'm dressed like some [%*!#] I don't like".Similarly in "Burden of Life", we hear the hushed voice, the picked clean guitar, the fuller band sound enters with drum and bass, becoming elegiac as the clean guitar lead sings- all of which concerns what sounds like a person on his/her deathbed aware of being unaware, bearing the burden of life and wishing to drop it.One of those passages made me think of my dad on his deathbed- after years of polio and later post-polio which eventually rendered him nearly immobile, and the devastating lyrics, "you knew an end was coming to the/ steady roll of your stride/ through golden beams falling from/ the sky/ you trampled down the doubt/ anyone could see in you the hope to/ lose that trouble close behind".My father did limp- gracefully- through golden beams falling from the sky, and was ready, oh, so ready to release the burden of life, the trouble close behind.Title TrackSo, I feel like posting ALL the lyrics on this track, they're that revealing, and tough, and tender, explanatory, and difficult.Which is one reason "Cold In Cold Out" is my favorite song of this outstanding EP- that plus the way it begins with a gentle classical guitar backing Harrison's most vulnerable vocals? then it grows, and grows, and builds.Let these lyrics suffice: "The path is a tangle of flowers and thorns/ of those who would bleed you/ and those who seem warm/ together you roam/ (CHORUS 1) and follow the light/ over the ground/ you ferry your bones/ all secretly asking/ when can we put the load down?"It struck me that the gorgeous full moon pictured is yet a reflection of the light of the sizzling sun, the life-giving sun. The journey is not without light; still, it is a journey with one final destination.The heart-wrenching chorus has three iterations, each more intense, building into almost unbearable loveliness and tragedy, in which Mr. Harrison shows his incredible vocal range, and we hear some cool bass guitar work after chorus two.We also get some gutsy power chords as an exquisite counterpoint to the gentle classical guitar.When can we put this load down? Cold in cold out.No HealerTime heals all wounds? Not this wound, no. Although I don't think of this EP as a single-concept album, it certainly has congruent threads, and as the final track, this one leaves a rather dark energy trailing.Although at first we hear, "no healer will come but the passage of time", later the narrator changes it to this: "no healer will come through the passage of time." On this track there are suggestions of dissonance in the swirling electric guitar passages, and the trippy lead guitar lines can seem almost dizzying.I've noticed in Doug Harrison's music a deep tie with the natural world, suggesting that all are tied into one long cord of life and death, living and dying. On "No Healer", we get the suggestion that the dying traveler becomes food and fuel for other species- and in this way, perhaps, life goes on.The light is shining, and the darkness does not comprehend it.In ConclusionIn short order, Doug Harrison via his side project, SLUG COMPARISON, returns with this stellar EP, set to release 09/10/2026- because of its lyrical depth and musical ingenuity, I consider this an excellent addition to any progressive rock collection.
items._cn_summary: 这张EP由加拿大音乐人Doug Harrison以个人项目形式发行，被归类为交叉前卫摇滚。专辑共六首曲目，总时长约二十七分钟。乐评以高度文学化的笔触将作品定位为关于死亡、心痛、背叛与微弱希望的冥想，音乐与歌词紧密咬合，旋律沉郁而富有层次。Harrison以人声为核心，搭配吉他、贝斯与编程，鼓手Randall Stoll参与录制。乐评大量篇幅聚焦于专辑封面意象、个人回忆与歌词片段的解读，暗示听众需反复品味才能把握其情感密度。从风格上看，该作品偏向艺术化但落点传统的摇滚创作，与实验、前卫、爵士、电子等口味交集有限，区域特征亦不明显，整体呈现为私语式、低调但成熟的独立摇滚写作。

items.body: The Copenhagen-based Institute for the Criminally Insane (ICI) and Danish dark synth act ee:man release the EBM/electro-industrial single “Born to Ride..” on August 14, 2026 through Tinnitorturous. The digital single arrives on major streaming and download services, with a lossless version on both acts’ Bandcamp pages. It is the second collaboration single by Institute for the Criminally Insane and ee:man, following “The Fabric of You..”. “Born to Ride..” addresses taking a fall, making a turn and getting back on your feet, set to music that is slower and darker than its predecessor. The cover was designed by Bo Heidelberg. ‘Born to Ride..’ follows ICI and ee:man’s ‘The Fabric of You..’ Institute for the Criminally Insane and ee:man first paired up on “The Fabric of You..”, released on Tinnitorturous. “Born to Ride..” carries the collaboration forward with a heavier, more subdued arrangement than the earlier single. Both acts’ back catalogues, including ICI’s “Gekippt” and ee:man’s “Bite the Hand,” remain available on their respective Bandcamp pages. About Institute for the Criminally Insane Institute for the Criminally Insane formed in Copenhagen in 1988. The project released its first compilation of demos, “Demo,” in 1990, followed by the EP “Audiotherapy” in 1993 and the album “Gekippt” in 1994, both through the now-defunct Danish label Decay Records. “Gekippt” became a cult album internationally, and its track “Slasher” was used in the video game “Hitman: Blood Money.” Institute for the Criminally Insane originally consisted of Bo Heidelberg and Kim G. Hansen. Bo Heidelberg reignited the project in 2020 and was briefly joined by Simon Holm before continuing as a one-man project. Institute for the Criminally Insane is currently working on material for release on Tinnitorturous and the Australian label Lightarmour Editions. ee:man is the Danish dark synth act of a producer who debuted in 2021 with the album “Echoes of Life,” built on melancholy synth chords and industrial undertones, and has been compared to Recoil, the solo project of Depeche Mode’s Alan Wilder. In recent years ee:man has moved toward EBM and industrial territory through collaborations with acts including In Absentia and Negant, and previously released the single “Bite the Hand” in January 2026. His darker material appears on Tinnitorturous, a Danish label run by Jens B. Petersen (ManMindMachine, Negant) and Tommy B-Kuhlmann (In Absentia, Negant, Body-Banden), while his lighter synth pop work is released through Town & Towers Records. “Born to Ride..” marks the second collaboration single between Institute for the Criminally Insane and ee:man.
items._cn_summary: 本文为Side-Line发布的单曲新闻稿，报道哥本哈根项目Institute for the Criminally Insane与丹麦暗潮合成器艺人ee:man合作的第二支单曲。曲目延续电子工业与暗潮氛围，节奏较前作更缓慢阴郁，编曲更厚重内敛。唱片由Bo Heidelberg操刀封面设计，通过丹麦独立厂牌Tinnitorturous发行数字版与无损Bandcamp版本。文章同时提供了两位艺人的背景资料，包括ICI自1988年以来的发展历程及其经典专辑在游戏配乐中的运用，以及ee:man从忧郁合成器流行向EBM工业领域转型的轨迹。作为一篇以发行信息为主的公告式报道，缺乏对音乐本体深入的评论与鉴赏。

items.body: Finnish Electronic Punk duo I Think I Broke Something releases the single “Illegal” on August 6. The track is the first single from the duo’s upcoming EP “Another Escape,” due November 5 on the same day as a release show at Semifinal in Helsinki. Illegal by I Think I Broke Something “Illegal” continues the sound the duo has built its catalog on, pairing electronic production with heavier, metal-weighted instrumentation. “Illegal continues ITIBS’s signature blend of explosive electronics and metal-heavy weight. Someone once described our sound as The Prodigy on steroids. And this track probably sounds exactly like that,” the band states. ‘Illegal’ leads into ‘Another Escape’ and a Helsinki release show “Illegal” is the first taste of “Another Escape,” the duo’s next EP, out November 5. The band will mark the EP’s release the same day with a show at Semifinal in Helsinki. Sonically, “Illegal” sits alongside prior ITIBS singles such as “Raw” and “Corpse”, continuing a distorted electronic hybrid the band places somewhere between The Prodigy, 3TEETH and Nine Inch Nails. About I Think I Broke Something I Think I Broke Something, also known as ITIBS, is a Helsinki-based duo made up of Jouni and Miika, active since 2014. The project debuted with the EP “Superman Sabotage Clan” and has since released three full-length albums, including “Still Not Going To” on October 26, 2022, alongside numerous singles and remixes through various labels. Prior singles from that album cycle included “Astral” and “All Is Not,” the latter remixed by drum’n’bass and metal producer Zardonic. The duo has also worked with The Prodigy’s Maxim and DJ Hyper. ITIBS describes its sound as a distorted electronic hybrid drawing on The Prodigy, Skinny Puppy and 3TEETH, mixing explosive electronics with metal-heavy weight. “Illegal,” released August 6, extends that catalog and leads into the EP “Another Escape,” due November 5 alongside the band’s release show at Semifinal in Helsinki.

items.body: Eye New Dark, the synthpop and darkwave solo project of Null Device vocalist and keyboardist Jill Sheridan, released the five-track EP “Adore” digitally on 4 August 2026 via Bandcamp. The EP follows Sheridan’s description of the project as built on “dark melodies, synthy beats.” Adore by Eye New Dark ‘Adore’ tracklist and prior single “Adore” contains five tracks: “More than Perfect,” “Real Life,” “Backwards Through That Door,” “A-D-O-R-E” and “Eyes in the Dark.” The third track previously appeared as a standalone single, “Backwards Through That Door,” released 30 June 2026 with two remixes: one by Klack and one by Null Device. Those remixes are not included on “Adore,” which presents the original version of the song alongside four new tracks. “Adore” is Eye New Dark’s second release. Sheridan introduced the project in May 2024 with the four-track “Tell Me / Smile My Dear,” which also carried remixes from Klack and Null Device. About Eye New Dark Eye New Dark is the solo project of Jill Sheridan, who has served as keyboardist, vocalist, songwriter and producer in Null Device since the Madison, Wisconsin band’s founding in 1995 by University of Wisconsin students Eric Oehler, Eric Goedken and Sheridan herself. Null Device moved from instrumental electronic music toward the romantic, New Order-referencing synthpop that has defined the band since, signing to Nilaihah Records in 2002 and releasing a run of albums that incorporated Arabic and Indian instrumentation before the label’s dissolution. The band went on to self-release two further records and later signed to Distortion Productions, issuing “While You Were Otherwise Engaged” in December 2016 and the eighth album, “The Emerald Age”, in November 2022. Sheridan launched Eye New Dark alongside her continuing role in Null Device, debuting the project in May 2024 with “Tell Me / Smile My Dear.” “Adore,” released in August 2026, is the project’s first five-track EP and its second overall release. No Wikipedia entry or Discogs profile exists yet specifically for Eye New Dark.

items.body: August has landed, and Dutch summer firmly has me in it’s clammy paws. As I sit here, sweating out an unseasonable bout of some mysterious illness, a chilling, forest-dwelling revenant beckons. Seeking solace in the shade of mist-shrouded pines, I accept her invitation and am transported from the muggy heat of these low lands to the forests of the Pacific Northwest. Folk and death metal infused black metal project Hulder is her name, and her frontwoman Marliese Beeuwsaert has taken this journey physically. Since starting the project in 2018, she has moved across the Atlantic— leaving Belgium for the PNW—and added bassist/shared vocalist Necreon to the bands official line-up.Hulder’s previous record Verses in Oath (2024) briefly drew me into its orbit based on some favourable coverage in my regular haunts, and then quite quickly disappeared back behind the treeline, leaving impressions of some inspired riffs and passages and an unusually meaty, Swedeath-leaning guitar tone. It lacked a certain melodic memorability and iconic key moments to latch onto, and while at first I suspected these might shimmer into perspective out of the gloam on repeat listens, such revelation never descended from the canopy. It was with intrigue but tempered expectations that I embarked upon the dark and crooked woodland paths of Verbolgen (which according to sources translates to "Incensed", although that lacks a certain simmering resentfulness; I’d go for something in between that, like resentful, and spiteful).After a neither offensive nor particularly memorable intro, Hulder come out of the gate quite strong, with opening one-two punch “The Crowning” and “Thy Binding Oath” showing the band's fresh shoots of folk instrumentation, still supported by dark, rhythmic undergrowth and thick, gnarled trunks of riffs, vocals howling through the branches like a biting north wind. To my mild disappointment, however, the album’s promising start loses its footing and stumbles over hidden roots and in musty burrows. As soon as the tracks revert to shorter, faster and more blackened fare, they land unfortunately between melodic and biting, offering neither grandiose mysticism nor blistering assault. Around the album’s halfway point, the moonlit clearing that opens “In Blood and in Earth” and leads toward a more deliberate, slower movement shows significant promise, although the track and Verbolgen as a whole remain rooted in a similar issue as Verses in Oath was. These albums are certainly very well performed and produced, and clearly feature a personal touch being themed around Belgian folklore and adorned with multilingual lyrics.The album's second half features some glimmers of tantalizing starlight, most notably on the vicious riffs and melodic developments of “Den Nacht Zijn Lied” ("Night’s Song") which may hold up as the strongest track. “View From Nemeton” has some strong moments, and “A Beacon From Darkened Skies” comes perhaps closest to the kind of grand and layered melodic payoff that I expect from an album in this style. The interesting closing bonus track “Zonnesteen” ("Sunstone") leans hard into acoustic folk sensibilities, but unfortunately fails to weave their strands into a satisfying wreath with which to adorn the finished product. Whatever lingers in between the tracks I’ve mentioned unfortunately fails to become more than tantalizing silhouettes in the mist. Having traversed its sylvan bounds, Verbolgen was a bit of a frustrating album to review. Stylistically it ticks all my boxes, the production is excellent, and musicians both new and old, guest and permanent show they have what it takes. Hulder have clearly been hard at work further carving out their sound without endangering its promising heartwood. Yet, capitalizing on that promise with an album full of songs whose resin sticks to the soul as much as it smells inviting remains tantalisingly out of reach on Verbolgen, just as it did on Verses in Oath. I fear this album will also slip out of rotation soon, although I intend to give it some more time to gestate. Perhaps when the seasons change, it will appear favorable in dwindling light.  Verbolgen by Hulder

items.body:
Since everyone else has written something about the centennials of Miles Davis and John Coltrane, why not join the parade? It is a good opportunity to look at the timeline of bassists the legendary trumpeter and saxophonist used. Born just under four months apart, the pair worked together under the elder Davis’ name periodically between Fall 1955 and Spring 1957 before a more steady affiliation in 1958-1960.

It is in that latter period that this analysis will begin, as it gives a convenient bit of serendipity: the fact that two of the their most famed albums were made in that period, Davis’ Kind Blue (March 2nd and April 22nd, 1959 for Columbia) and Coltrane’s Giant Steps (May 4th–5th and December 2nd, 1959). And the analysis will end with Coltrane’s death in 1967, which came during the tenure of Davis’ “second great quintet” and before his groups swelled and electrified during his fusion period.

As such, we begin with the same man, the bassist on both those albums: Paul Chambers. He had taken up the bass a decade earlier in his adopted home of Detroit (where he was a student at the seminal Cass Technical High School ... more on that later). He arrived in New York in 1954 at 19. By the time of Kind of Blue and Giant Steps, he had been on over 100 sessions from dozens of leaders, with multiple dates under Davis (with whom he had started working in late 1955) and Coltrane (who had used him for several albums in 1957-58 as well as both fellow sideman for many others and Chambers also hiring Coltrane for his own sessions). In addition to the five albums he led, Chambers played on sessions for Benny Golson, Curtis Fuller, J.J. Johnson, Lee Morgan, Red Garland, Sonny Clark, and Sonny Rollins.

The collaboration between Davis and Chambers was remarkably fruitful before and after Kind of Blue and solidified a part of Davis’ music that had previously seen widely differing players like Tommy Potter, Oscar Pettiford, Al McKibbon, and Percy Heath. The rest of 1959 saw multiple engagements around the country and closed with recordings that would be part of another monumental record, Sketches of Spain, that paired Davis’ group with the Gil Evans Orchestra. 1960 continued that momentum with more Sketches of Spain recording and almost non-stop touring, including two stretches in Europe, from Spring onward. 1961 and 1962 had more of the same activity, the documents being Someday My Prince Will Come and Quiet Nights. Then, quite suddenly, Chambers left Davis’ group in early February 1963.

It should be stated that Chambers did not restrict his activities solely to Davis, recording over four dozen albums during the period with, among many others, Jackie McLean, Wynton Kelly, Benny Golson, Hank Mobley, and Curtis Fuller. And after leaving Davis, he worked steadily with an array of leaders through the end of 1968, sadly passing away from tuberculosis caused and/or aggravated by drug abuse at only 33.

Stepping right into the Davis group was another Cass Technical High School alumnus: Ron Carter. Nearly 26, Carter was already prophesying his prolific career, participating in over three dozen albums since 1960, with the likes of Charli Persip, Yusef Lateef, Eric Dolphy, Don Ellis, Coleman Hawkins, Cecil Payne, Jaki Byard, Wes Montgomery, Bobby Timmons, Tadd Dameron, Dizzy Reece, Ken McIntyre, Milt Jackson, Benny Golson and others, plus waxing his leader debut, Where?, for Prestige subsidiary New Jazz in 1961.

It was Carter’s arrival that heralded Davis’ soon-to-be seminal band, though it took until Fall 1964 for its personnel to solidify. With Carter, Davis recorded Seven Steps To Heaven and played the Antibes festival in 1963. What is interesting though is while the “second great quintet” is thought of as a monolith, the bass chair had some upheaval/fluidity, depending on how you look at it. Gary Peacock – already a veteran and likely the only person to work for both Bud Shank and Albert Ayler – took the chair for nearly six weeks in the spring of 1964, Carter returning thereafter through the end of the year. 1965 began auspiciously with the January recording of E.S.P. but then things derailed with a convalescing Davis unable to play. And when he could, in November and December, Carter, a hot commodity, was absent, spelled by Peacock once more, then Reggie Workman, who had come up around the same time as Carter and had already come and gone in the groups of Coltrane. In 1966, Carter would return to the group but only partially, participating in East Coast performances, shows elsewhere having either Richard Davis, Carter’s only real equal in terms of fecundity, or in the Peacock mold of eclecticism, Eddie Gomez, returning permanently in October, just before the album Miles Smiles. 1967 was similar: Carter was on board when not busy elsewhere, Gomez on call, then Albert Stinson for one show (a little over two years before his passing – see Bass Tragedies column in Issue 94) and then another veteran, Buster Williams, for a tour (and playing on one track of the 1981-released compilation album Directions). Carter would fill a fixed point for all of 1967, including the albums Sorcerer and Nefertiti and would continue with Davis through the middle of 1968.

Like Chambers or perhaps even more so, Carter was also on the greater jazz scene during his tenure with Davis. He recorded on sessions led by his fellow Davis bandmates but also by everyone from Bobby Timmons, Charles Lloyd, Donald Byrd and Bobby Hutcherson to Jimmy Smith, Shirley Scott, Eddie Harris, and Stanley Turrentine, to name only a handful. He has, of course, gone on to be likely the most recorded bassist in jazz history.

Paul Chambers’ time under Coltrane was shorter and more intermittent. After Giant Steps he was part of, along with the rest of Davis’ period band, November 1959 recordings that would partly comprise Coltrane Jazz and be brought back 18 months later as one of three individual bassists taking part in the Africa/Brass recordings (though his contribution was only heard on the 1995 complete sessions version).

Also in 1959 was a Birdland engagement for Coltrane where either Ahmed Abdul-Malik or George Tucker, both established and close in age to Coltrane, were on bass.

In 1960 Coltrane hired the slightly younger Steve Davis in what seems to be his first professional engagement. Davis stayed in the band through the end of the year for all its live dates and played on music recorded in October and released piecemeal on My Favorite Things, Coltrane Jazz, Coltrane Plays the Blues, and Coltrane’s Sound. Though Davis lived until 1987, his credits after Coltrane were slight: the Mangione Brothers, Dave Burns, McCoy Tyner, Kenny Dorham, James Moody, Freddie McCoy, and Eddie Jefferson, all made in the ‘60s. One deviation in the year came via Coltrane’s shared date with Don Cherry, The Avant-Garde, where bass was handled by either Charlie Haden or Percy Heath.

1961 was a year in flux, bassist-wise, for Coltrane. He introduced a concept to which he would return later in the decade by using two bassists for an engagement at Chicago’s Sutherland Lounge in March: Raphael Don Garrett and Workman, the former, about six years younger, working with Roland Kirk, Paul Serrano, and Eddie Harris, the latter 11 years younger, sideman for Gigi Gryce, Donald Byrd, Duke Jordan, Richard Williams, and Dave Pike.

Workman would be part of the aforementioned Africa/Brass, as would, separately, another bassist, Art Davis, already with credits under Max Roach, Lee Morgan, Booker Little, Hal Mooney, Ernestine Anderson, Dizzy Gillespie, Leo Wright, Clifford Jordan/Sonny Red, Abbey Lincoln, and Booker Little. But in May they were together for Ole Coltrane and nearly a month at the Village Vanguard in August. Workman would become the fixed bassist for Coltrane through the end of the year for concerts, including a European tour, and a small portion of the Ballads album from the end of the year. An exception was Workman either alternating or alongside Jimmy Garrison for a November stint at the Village Vanguard.

If not for a family health crisis forcing Workman to leave the group at the end of 1961 and return to his native Philadelphia, he likely would have stayed with the band and jazz history been quite different. It should be said that Workman hardly is a footnote, becoming one of the most revered players of his generation. But it was Garrison who became the anchor. Born between Garrett and Workman, prior to joining Coltrane he had worked with Philly Joe Jones, Curtis Fuller, Kenny Dorham, Jackie McLean, JR Montrose, Walter Bishop, Jr., Ornette Coleman, Bill Barron, and Ted Curson.

Unlike Carter and Davis, once Garrison was on board, he stayed there. That was mostly to do with Coltrane’s packed schedule of touring and albums and that, unlike Davis, he was healthy and non-combustible. From 1962-1964, Garrison was omnipresent, including the bulk of Ballads, Duke Ellington & John Coltrane (where he split duties with Ellington’s period bassist Aaron Bell), 2018 discovery Both Directions At Once, John Coltrane And Johnny Hartman, Impressions, Crescent, another new millennium unearthed gem in Blue World, and closing out the year with Coltrane’s magnum opus A Love Supreme (which added Art Davis for a second day of recording, released as a second disc to the album’s deluxe edition in 2002).

In 1965 Garrison was still the main man but occasionally Davis would be alongside him: partially on The John Coltrane Quartet Plays in February and fully for June’s Ascension. Otherwise, Garrison was the sole bassist for performances and most of the other albums: Transition, Sun Ship, and Meditations. The exceptions without Davis were overdubs of Haden for the posthumously released Infinity and Garrett returning to play both bass and clarinet for Live In Seattle (as well as the 2021 archival release A Love Supreme: Live In Seattle), Om, and part of Kulu Se Mama.

1966 was even more Garrison-centric, with the only documented work including a second bassist shows in November and December with Lionel “Sonny” Johnson, the brother of Dewey Johnson, who had played on Ascension. The last year of Coltrane’s life, Garrison was there as well, with one notable absence: the Coltrane/Rashied Ali duet Interstellar Space.

Unlike Chambers or Carter, Garrison was kept so busy during his time with Coltrane that his outside discography at the time is meager, though it does include his sole leader date, Illumination! with the Elvin Jones/Jimmy Garrison Sextet. Otherwise it was sessions with Lorez Alexandria, Coltrane bandmate McCoy Tyner, Sonny Rollins, Bill Dixon, and Robert F. Pozar.

After Coltrane’s death, Garrison kept working but his documentation slowed, his two Blue Note dates with the Jones trio rounded out by Joe Farrell being the most enduring. There were also dates with Rolf and Joachim Kuhn, Clifford Thornton and Nathan Davis, and regular work with Alice Coltrane and Archie Shepp. His final recording came in early 1975 with Beaver Harris and Dave Burrell’s 360 Degree Music Experience. Garrison died of lung cancer in 1976 at 42.

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items._cn_summary: 这张现场专辑记录了Dr. John（Malcolm Mac Rebennack Jr.）1999年在德国洛雷莱露天剧场的演出，由西德意志广播公司WDR的长期音乐节目Rockpalast录制发行。乐队阵容包括吉他手Bobby Broom、贝斯手David Barard和鼓手Herman Ernest，均为新奥尔良乐坛老将。演出曲目以新奥尔良经典为主，融合R&B、放克、布鲁斯与爵士元素，开场为传统Mardi Gras名曲《Iko Iko》，随后演绎Dr. John标志性的巫毒风格代表作《I Walk on Guilded Splinters》，以及《Right Place, Wrong Time》等热门曲目，并以Earl King的《Big Chief》收尾。整场演出呈现出浓厚的美国南方音乐传统与Mardi Gras庆典氛围。

items.body: Review by Aussie-Byrd-Brother — Nearly sixty years into their existence, legendary rock band Yes may never recapture that dynamic, extravagant and inspired edge that made them one of the defining prog-rock bands of the Seventies, but that doesn't mean there's nothing left of worth with the current line-up and their recent releases. Mostly driven by longtime guitarist Steve Howe, here aided by frequent contributors - keyboardist Geoff Downes, bass player Billy Sherwood, former Glass Hammer frontman Jon Davison and more recent drummer Jan Schellen - this incarnation of the symphonic institution (having navigated the loss of founding bassist Chris Squire and longtime drummer Alan White) returns with their fourth album together, and twenty-sixth studio work overall, 2026's `Aurora', that shows them still offering colourful, adventurous and melodic rock that many die-hard fans will enjoy.Title track `Aurora' is a glorious and slick opener, where fancy orchestration, calling to mind their 2001 Album `Magnification', swoons around Steve Howe's reaching guitar strains, Billy Sherwood honouring the tradition of the late Chris Squire's upfront bass rumbles and a flighty Jon Davison vocal. Joyful with rousing reprises of striking themes, it makes for a memorable and impressive opener about evoking transformation and connection, and damned if "Like paper doves in a cut-out world..." ain't a darn adorable lyric!Despite lovely group harmonies and little pockets of fancy instrumental touches, `Turnaround Situation' doesn't hold together particularly well as a whole, but there's lovely buoyant bass and fancy acoustic flourishes racing alongside each-other throughout the dreamy and romantic (and better) `Love Lies Dreaming', perhaps vocally and musically one of the prettiest pieces of the disc.Being the longest track on the album at near fourteen minutes will instantly pique the interest of most prog-rock fans, but...lower that eyebrow, mister! Sadly the four-part `Countermovement', contemplating human authenticity, comes across as more a collection of fragments and half-completed passages rather than a coherent and flowing whole, but there are a nice range of tempo-shifts back and forth, and a lot of focus put on both Steve Howe's humble and pensive vocal and a range of versatile guitar solo spots.With `Ariadne', Yes adopts a storytelling approach of so many prog bands old and new, looking to myth and legend for inspiration, and it suitably surges forwards with Jan's strident drumming and delicate orchestration that soars with classical fancy. At its heart it recounts the mythological Greek tale of Princess Ariadne and the Minotaur's labyrinth, which the band also uses it as a metaphor for being lost, with lines like "With walls around you, you're trapped in your own space", and finally taking control. Howe's guitar adds a heroic flavour and urgency, and it's nice to hear group harmonies from several members together throughout.Despite a fairly banal lyric about springing to action, `All Hands on Deck' is quite fun with jaunty keyboard/guitar interplay, made memorable by Steve's guitar grunt that takes on a bluesier toughness in little bursts, and it's nice to hear Jon singing a little more naturally deeper throughout too! In what could probably be considered an interlude, the three minute `Outside the Box' is primarily an instrumental. Framed by a constantly morphing set of wordless sighing group harmonies, they're interspersed with an eclectic grab-bag of fuzzy electronic swirls, jamming bass/guitar duels and intricate drum patterns across a range of tempos back and forth.Short and sweet, soft-rocker `Emotional Intelligence' opens with gentle piano, unassuming acoustic strums and the warm hum of Hammond organ, Davison softly offering a call to understanding and unity with its well-meaning lyric. It briefly springs up to life near its climax with slide guitar wisps, and this compact little album closer displays restraint and tastefulness throughout.All versions of `Aurora' come with two pieces that are classed as bonus tracks, but they are actually both worthwhile inclusions that don't disrupt the flow of the core album or come across as mere throwaways. `Jambustin' (really just a fun way to refer to being `cut off'), is a warning against negative behaviours and arguing with or obstructing others, displaying a jauntiness in its verses and a softly grooving chorus with slinking bass. Despite a fairly overused motive of moving water as a metaphor for life and the passing of time, `Watching the River Roll' embraces the theme with acceptance and peace, and it delivers dreamy and shimmering instrumentation (not to mention constantly drifting Moog solos!) and bristles with an upbeat, life-affirming positivity that glides with energy.Yes has always had more to offer than just the contributions of former vocalist Jon Anderson and keyboardist Rick Wakeman, and modern, worthwhile work from both of those artists can easily be found elsewhere, so their absence doesn't take anything away from this current version of the group. Some pockets of the fanbase will find their exclusion absolutely inexcusable, meaning there's no coming back from that, but Yes has constantly had an eclectic revolving door of imaginative, skilled and varied musicians that have all made exciting contributions to the overall Yes sound throughout the decades.Despite being a little overlong and delivering a couple of less successful pieces, Yes have delivered an enjoyable disc of vibrant and eclectic rock in `Aurora', always melodic without falling into overtly poppy or radio-friendly banality and full of interesting instrumental details. Given several re-spins, it proves to be valid addition to the Yes legacy, with the current incarnation looking to their past but still moving forward in interesting and rewarding ways, and if you appreciate the wider world of Yes music from a range of musicians, chances are you'll find much to enjoy here.Three and a half stars.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是传奇老牌前卫摇滚乐队成立近六十年后的第二十六张录音室作品，延续了由吉他手Steve Howe主导的当前阵容。专辑以管弦乐编排与吉他交织为主轴，开篇同名曲将华丽管弦乐铺底与吉他音色结合，旋律流畅且结构完整。另含抒情向的梦幻曲目，编曲较为甜美。长达十四分钟的多段式作品尝试构建宏大叙事，但被评论指出更像是片段拼贴而非有机整体。另有一曲取材希腊神话米诺陶迷宫，以管弦乐与鼓击推进，讲述迷失与自控的主题。整体而言，这是一张面向老牌乐队忠实听众的怀旧向制作，在管弦乐与摇滚乐融合层面有一定编排功底，但在声音设计与创新性上趋于保守，与实验、前卫融合或电子等当代边界领域交集甚少。

items.body: Here’s one we missed. French electro-rock duo Marigold has made its debut album, “Noir Boulevard”, available on all major streaming platforms since 20 May 2026. The band mixes new wave, electronic tension and rock energy, describing its own sound as sitting between Depeche Mode and M83. Marigold blends new wave and rock energy on ‘Noir Boulevard’ The duo describes its music as “a powerful and immersive sonic universe, blending new wave, electronic tension, and rock energy,” built on live experience the duo traces back to the early 2000s. “Noir Boulevard” is the pair’s first full-length release and marks Side-Line’s first coverage of the project. About Marigold Marigold is a French electro-rock duo whose sound draws on new wave, electronic and rock elements, with the band itself citing Depeche Mode and M83 as reference points. The project maintains an official YouTube channel, “Marigold ϟ,” which lists Montpellier, France as its base and describes the act’s style with the tags electro, rock, synthwave, coldwave, darkwave and new wave. The duo has extensive live experience dating back to the early 2000s. Its debut album, “Noir Boulevard,” became available on all major streaming platforms on 20 May 2026.
items._cn_summary: 法国二人组合 Marigold 首张专辑《Noir Boulevard》于2026年5月20日登陆各主流流媒体平台。自定位介于Depeche Mode与M83之间，将新浪潮、电子张力与摇滚能量融为一体，乐器编制和制作手法偏主流方向。乐队成员拥有自2000年代初以来的丰富现场经验积累，作品据称呈现出沉浸式的声音宇宙。YouTube频道显示其风格标签涵盖electro、synthwave、coldwave与darkwave等元素。虽然涉及暗潮与电子交叉地带，但整体定位更接近易于接受的电摇风格，在声音实验性和先锋性上缺乏突出表现。文章内容为信息性新闻稿，对专辑具体音乐细节、编曲手法与艺术创新方面几乎没有实质性讨论，可获取的评估信息极为有限。

items.body: Futurepop act Assemblage 23 has announced a five-date European headline tour for October 2026, with Mari Kattman joining as special guest on every date. Tom Shear will bring material from the album “Null” to club venues in Germany and Sweden. Null by Assemblage 23 The tour follows summer festival appearances for Assemblage 23, including a performance at Amphi Festival. “Null,” the project’s tenth studio album, was released via Metropolis Records on 7 November 2025. Mari Kattman, joining all headline dates as special guest, is known for her solo work as well as her role in Helix, her ongoing collaboration with Tom Shear, and mastering work for numerous artists across the industrial, EBM and synthpop scenes. Tour dates for Assemblage 23 Assemblage 23 plays the following dates in October 2026, with Mari Kattman as special guest throughout: 20 October – Karlsruhe, Germany – Die Stadtmitte 21 October – Oberhausen, Germany – Kulttempel 22 October – Hamburg, Germany – Indra Musikclub 23 October – Jonkoping, Sweden – SektorF 24 October – Hannover, Germany – SubKultur About Assemblage 23 Assemblage 23 is the American electro-industrial and futurepop project of Tom Shear, who debuted with the album “Contempt” in 1999. “Failure” followed in 2001 and found traction in dance clubs, before Shear signed to Metropolis Records and released “Defiance” in 2002 and “Storm” in 2003. The 2007 album “Meta” produced the single “Binary,” which reached the Top 25 of the Billboard U.S. singles chart, and was followed by “Compass” in 2009, “Bruise” in 2012, “Endure” in 2016 and “Mourn” in 2020. In 2018, Shear launched Helix, a side project with vocalist Mari Kattman that blends electronics, organic instrumentation and vocal harmonies across trip-hop, dub, dream pop and synthpop influences. Kattman, based in Providence, Rhode Island, has also lent vocals to acts including Mesh, Psy’Aviah, iVardensphere, Aesthetische, Neuroticfish and Solitary Experiments, and released her own material through COP International and Metropolis Records. Assemblage 23 released its tenth studio album, “Null,” via Metropolis Records on 7 November 2025, preceded by the singles “Tolerate” and “Believe.” The October 2026 European tour, with Kattman as support on every date, brings “Null” to club audiences in Germany and Sweden following the band’s summer festival run.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是越南裔美国创作人Kelly Truong的第二张作品，由纽约独立厂牌Bayonet发行。乐评将音乐定位为表面梦幻流畅、实则暗藏深度的风格，情感释放偏向内敛与沉思，而非激烈爆发。创作人以CD时代的怀旧美学为根基，从橙郡移居洛杉矶后逐步构建个人声音。专辑在悦耳旋律与情绪层次之间寻求平衡，融合了独立流行的可听性与内省气质，试图在商业可达性与艺术深度之间找到契合点。作为独立厂牌的中等规模制作，它既非纯粹的主流流行，也未深入实验领域，呈现出一种温和而克制的表达方式。

items.body: Los Angeles electro-pop duo Tart Vandelay releases its debut album, “Odyssey”, independently on August 7, 2026, on all streaming platforms. The record, made by musical couple Kate Halligan and Marty LoFaso, brings together eleven tracks written and developed over nearly ten years. Halligan stated: “This album is almost like a child to us. It grew up alongside us. Each song captures a different phase of our lives, our relationship, and our evolution as artists and as people. It’s about sharing our art and spreading good vibes to our audience.” LoFaso stated: “Odyssey is proof that it’s worth patiently pursuing a dream. We’re incredibly happy to finally present this first chapter of our story.” ‘Spin,’ ‘Bells’ and ‘Starlight’ lead into ‘Odyssey’ Tart Vandelay built up to “Odyssey” with a run of singles, each presenting a different side of the duo’s sound. “Spin” and “Bells” arrived first, followed by “Starlight,” the final single before the album and, according to the band, the song that ended up setting the creative direction for the whole record. “Starlight” combines synthesizers and pop melodies in an arrangement that balances retro-leaning tones with contemporary production. Across “Odyssey,” the duo mixes synth-pop, electronic indie and contemporary disco into a single identity. “Bells,” the most recent single before “Odyssey,” is available to stream below. About Tart Vandelay Tart Vandelay formed in 2014 when Kate Halligan and Marty LoFaso began writing songs together while studying in Boston; the pair transferred to Berklee College of Music, where Halligan studied songwriting and LoFaso studied music business. The duo later moved to Halligan and LoFaso’s home region in the Northeast before relocating to Phoenix, Arizona, and eventually to Los Angeles, California, where they are now based. Along the way they released the EP “Janus” (2019) and singles including “Luv Who U R” (2021), “DJ Play My Song” (2021), “R U Mine?” (2022) and “I’m Dreaming” (2024), building an independent career around a sound that mixes synth-pop, electronic indie and contemporary disco. In 2026, the singles “Spin” and “Bells” led into “Starlight,” the final single ahead of “Odyssey,” the duo’s debut studio album, released independently on August 7, 2026.
items._cn_summary: 洛杉矶二人组Tart Vandelay于2026年8月独立发行首张专辑《Odyssey》，收录十一首曲目，由情侣档Kate Halligan与Marty LoFaso历经近十年创作完成。专辑以单曲"Spin""Bells""Starlight"为铺垫，据乐队称最终单曲"Starlight"确立了整张专辑的创作方向。该作品将合成器流行、电子独立与当代迪斯科风格融合在一起，在复古音色与当代制作之间寻求平衡。Halligan曾就读于伯克利音乐学院学习词曲创作，LoFaso则主修音乐商业。两人自2014年在波士顿开始合作，此后辗转凤凰城、洛杉矶等地，陆续发行EP《Janus》与多支单曲，逐步建立起独立音乐生涯。这是一张按部就班成长起来的独立流行作品，风格偏向主流受众可接受的电子流行范畴，在声音探索层面缺少具有突破性的实验意图与个人辨识度，与先锋路线相距较远。

items.body:
Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar.
Vanishment
contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina�s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice.
The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette.
Kerosene Madrigal
The range of backgrounds leads to many styles, and the record betrays interesting influences. The opening track, �Kerosene Madrigal,� is a sort of miner�s blues reminiscent of Michelle Shocked. The soul-country of �Imagined Love� reminded me of fellow Torontonians Cowboy Junkies, especially the sweet organ. The stoic and twangy �Don�t Fault the Stars for Falling� could have been a Dolly Parton tune.
A Grand Expanse
�A Grand Expanse� has a more ambitious arrangement.  It sounds like the end-credits song from a long-ago film we only vaguely remember. It says everything it needs to in one minute and twenty seconds and exactly 38 words. It is quintessential Tiny Sun.
The entire recording feels like music from a dream, and since no one knows exactly what dream music sounds like, this could be it.
Berceuse
Tiny Sun will perform the entire album at Toronto�s Koerner Hall on May 14, 2026.

items.body:
TUIDE are giving fans their first look at all seven members in action. The new girl group unveiled Meet my GRLS, TUIDE, their first performance video ahead of their official debut. The visual features 'GRLS', a track from their upcoming debut EP, TUNE & PLAY, which arrives on 24 August.

Made up of SEOHEE, SEOYEON, ELENA, JIA, SAKI, SEAH, and YI HANI, TUIDE are the first act from ABD, HYBE MUSIC GROUP’s new label specialising in girl group production.

Built around an energetic garage rhythm, 'GRLS' introduces the seven members one by one before bringing their individual personalities together through its recurring “Meet my girls / Me & my girls” hook. Its choreography draws from house, hip-hop, and soul, while the video moves between colourful interconnected spaces to spotlight each member.

According to the group, the song embodies what they call their “bestie-tude” — a confidence rooted in individuality and the friendship shared between the members, who hail from Korea, the U.S., the U.K., and Japan.

TUIDE take their name from the phrase “Tune the Tide,” reflecting the group’s ambition to transform the different “tides” they encounter into new forms of joy through music.

Like what you read? Show our writer some love!

-
items._cn_summary: 本文为HYBE新厂牌旗下女子组合TUIDE的出道预告新闻稿，介绍了七人组合的首支表演曲目《GRLS》。歌曲采用车库节奏基底，融合house、嘻哈与灵魂乐元素，编舞同样取自这三种风格。七位成员来自韩国、美国、英国和日本，歌曲传达所谓"bestie-tude"概念——以个人自信与友谊为核心。组合名称TUIDE源自"Tune the Tide"，寓意将不同文化背景转化为音乐喜悦。文章内容以成员介绍和概念阐述为主，缺乏对音乐制作、声音设计或编曲细节的深入分析，整体属于典型的商业偶像团体出道宣传稿，与实验、前卫或独立音乐审美距离较远。

items.body: The influential music producer played a key role in designing the sound of 90s records by Madonna and Blur William Orbit, the influential electronic music producer who designed the sound of classic records like Madonna's Ray Of Light, has died at the age of 69. "William passed away at home on 23rd July, 2026,” Orbit's family wrote in a statement shared on Instagram. "We are deeply saddened by his passing. He will be greatly missed by us and by so many whose lives he touched through his music, friendship, and kindness." A cause of death was not publicly revealed. Born William Wainwright in Enfield, North London in 1956, he dropped out of school at 16 and worked a variety of low-paying jobs while seeking... The post William Orbit has Died, Aged 69 appeared first on The Quietus.

items.body: Review by Chaoticreason — 2 stars,A most beautiful female vocalist pervades this music.However, I find the lack of detail to the nuances of musical detail, and also the use of a drum machine severely detract from my finding this album of any great worth. It would be difficult to recommend this album. I have no wish to put anybody down, but I just feel that not enough time, thought, and effort went into making this album, maybe money as well?It certainly has a degree of potentiality, but that all feels lost in the recording, of what could have been a pretty good album.I have listened to the whole album (ouch). It is not completely without merit, but I could not really see why anyone would pick this album out from so many other, more accomplished works that lie within this realm.I hate writing bad words about anybody. But it is painfully obvious that this could have been a way better album than it is. As it stands, this is not a well put together work, the use of a drum machine, (drum machines are okay in the right place) is a disaster. I don't wish to pick any further holes in this work, as that would be simply disrespectful. I have probably said enough already.

items.body: Review by XixoTheRock — Locande delle fate is a band which I had not heard of until an acquaintance of mine recommended themto me after chatting about prog and jazz for a while, evidently as I do, I postponed listening toany of their records until I finished some pending ones, now I have listened to this record, "HomoHomini Lupus" twice, and I'm eager to say the many things I think about this particular record,which, are not very positive if I'm to be very honest.I'd like to address that, I do not speak Italian, and while Spanish and Italian do share a ton ofgrammar, words and common origin from latin, I did not fully understand the lyrics because of thislanguage barrier, judging by the overview I did indeed understand, this is a concept album, which isapparent and obvious mainly by the track titles, despite this, I will not analyze the lyrical aspectof the record any further since I'm not in a position to do so.This record is quite different from your average RPI record in the sense that, it's notgrandiloquent, baroque, theatrical and Mediterranean sounding, I'd like to say that something thatmakes a record great is sticking to it's cultural roots and sound while innovating and expandingit's foundations...Homo Homini Lupus DOES NOT do that, it splits from the Italian roots that madeRPI great in the first place, and tries to mimic Anglo-Saxon rock and pop. The quality of thecompositions is very poor, the tracks are mostly bland and dull, nothing really fits completely, itsits in an uncanny valley : trying to mimic someone else while trying to pretend you have notabandoned your identity. The instruments are simple, just hour typical line up of some keys,guitars, bass guitars and drums, sometimes less is more, but this is not the case, they feeldisconnected both musically and emotionally...almost as a watered down Alan Parsons project, which Iwill asume was a big inspiration for Locanda delle fate's creative process.Despite the musicians and singer being very talented, they still feel plain, they sound as if theywere not motivated, the singer's high pitched vocals are also unbearable most of the time, they trybeing dramatic..maybe they tried TOO hard, and too much of anything is never any good.The production is also dull, not balanced, poorly equalized, inconsistent between tracks (whichworsens the fact that all songs, are almost the same in composition, and this productioninconsistency does not help at all), and the guitar tones are simply just too exaggerated.For the quality this record has, it could have been 10 or 15 minutes shorter and no one wouldcomplain really, it's a record that disappoints, specially since it is part of one of the best progsub genres...really, I wouldn't listen to it again, and I urge you that, if you want to listen toany other record by Locanda delle fate, follow the advice of other reviewers and avoid this record,go straight into their debut album.

items.body: Anthrax - Cursum Perficio Anthrax need no introduction. The New York Thrash Titans are set to release their 12th full-length studio album titled Cursum Perficio on September 18th via Nuclear Blast Records and Megaforce Records (North America). The phrase Cursum Perficio is Latin for âMy journey has come to an end,â âor âI complete my journey.â Itâs heartening to hear from the band themselves that the album title doesnât necessarily mean that this is Anthraxâs final album. Apparently it was chosen more for the fact that the band believe the album is a culmination of everything theyâve learned across their 40+ year career. Playing through the album its hard to argue with that statement. I look at Anthraxâs career in 3 parts. Their early Thrash era, where they released seminal Thrash metal albums like Spreading the Disease , Among the Living and Persistence of Time . The John Bush era, where the change in vocalists made the band a slightly different, yet still formidable act, adding classic albums such as the Sound of White Nosie and Weâve Come for You All to their cannon. Weâre now in the Joey reunion period. Itâs been a decade since 2016âs For All Kings , but as always Anthrax are prioritising quality over quantity in the twilight of their career. Cursum Perficio does sound like a true culmination of all three periods.

items.body: Dicas e truques de jogadores para Fortune Mouse Fortune Mouse é um jogo de caça-níqueis que tem conquistado a atenção de muitos jogadores devido à sua jogabilidade envolvente e potencial de ganhos. Para aqueles que desejam maximizar suas chances de sucesso, reunimos dicas valiosas de jogadores experientes que já testaram suas habilidades nesse emocionante jogo. Acompanhe nossas sugestões e descubra como aumentar suas chances de vitória. Conselhos práticos de quem já jogou Os jogadores que se destacam no Fortune Mouse frequentemente compartilham conselhos práticos que podem ser muito úteis para iniciantes. Um dos principais pontos mencionados é a importância de entender as mecânicas do jogo. Conhecer os símbolos, as linhas de pagamento e as funções especiais pode fazer toda a diferença. Além disso, muitos usuários recomendam que os jogadores façam uma análise detalhada do retorno ao jogador (RTP) do jogo, que é de aproximadamente 96,5%. Compreender essa taxa ajuda a planejar melhor as apostas. Outro conselho valioso é começar com apostas menores para se familiarizar com o jogo. Jogadores que adotam essa estratégia costumam ter uma curva de aprendizado mais suave e podem prolongar sua experiência de jogo sem arriscar grandes perdas iniciais. A prática leva à perfeição, e aos poucos, você se sentirá mais confiante para aumentar suas apostas e explorar os recursos bônus que o Fortune Mouse oferece. Muitos jogadores compartilham suas experiências e dicas em comunidades online, e uma delas é o site fortune-mouse-jogo.com.br, onde você pode encontrar insights valiosos. Estratégias de aposta eficazes Desenvolver uma estratégia de apostas sólida é fundamental para qualquer jogador que deseja se destacar no Fortune Mouse. Uma abordagem popular é a técnica de gerenciamento de bankroll. Defina um orçamento claro antes de começar a jogar e nunca ultrapasse esse limite. Isso não apenas ajuda a evitar perdas significativas, mas também garante uma experiência de jogo mais prazerosa. Além disso, muitos jogadores sugerem a utilização de apostas progressivas, onde você aumenta sua aposta após uma vitória e a diminui após uma perda. Essa técnica pode ajudar a maximizar os ganhos durante uma sequência vencedora e minimizar as perdas durante períodos de azar. Outro aspecto a considerar é a escolha do momento certo para jogar. Jogadores experientes recomendam jogar em horários menos movimentados para aumentar suas chances de conseguir um bom retorno. Como escolher o momento certo para jogar A escolha do momento de jogo pode influenciar sua experiência no Fortune Mouse. Muitos jogadores acreditam que jogar em horários de pico pode resultar em maior competição e, consequentemente, menor chance de vitória. Tente jogar em horários onde há menos atividade, como durante as manhãs ou em dias de semana, para aumentar suas chances de sucesso. Além disso, preste atenção nas promoções e bônus oferecidos pelos cassinos. Muitas vezes, os cassinos online fazem promoções específicas em determinados horários ou dias, o que pode proporcionar uma excelente oportunidade para maximizar seus ganhos. Fique atento a eventos especiais ou datas comemorativas, pois os cassinos costumam oferecer bônus extras que podem ser muito vantajosos. Planejando seu jogo em torno dessas promoções, você poderá potencializar sua experiência. Depoimentos de sucesso na comunidade A comunidade de jogadores de Fortune Mouse é repleta de histórias inspiradoras de sucesso. Muitos compartilham suas vitórias em fóruns e redes sociais, o que motiva novos jogadores a experimentar o jogo. Um dos relatos mais comuns é sobre como uma estratégia bem planejada resultou em grandes vitórias, especialmente ao aproveitar os recursos bônus durante o jogo. Além disso, os jogadores frequentemente destacam a importância de um jogo responsável e equilibrado. As histórias de sucesso não se limitam apenas aos ganhos, mas também incluem a experiência de jogo em si. Jogadores que conseguem manter o controle emocional e não deixar que as perdas afetem seu estado de espírito tendem a ter uma experiência mais gratificante e, muitas vezes, acabam obtendo melhores resultados a longo prazo.

items.body: 発行年：2026 版元：けはい出版 公式サイト：https://withdilemma.theshop.jp/items/141822340 『交差点で：デザイン、言語、経験』はビジュアルコミュニケーションデザイナー、環境活動家の平山みな美によるインタビュー集である。横浜を拠点とする独立出版社兼印刷所NEUTRAL COLORSの依頼で、彼女がオランダの文化施設で滞在制作を行なった際の成果物として制作された。 「主に気候変動、環境問題、ジェンダー不平等などに取り組む団体や企業のデザインを率先して引き受けている★1」平山であるが、そんな問題意識をこの滞在でも深めようと、取材対象との対話に際し「文化的な表象という言葉を聞いて、思い浮かべるオブジェクトを持ってきてほしい★2」と伝え、それをきっかけとした議論が同書には収められている。この「文化的な表象」というテーマはきわめて広範であり、話題が抽象的になってしまう可能性もあるだろう。しかし平山は具体的に対象を「名指す」よう提案することによって、その懸念を回避している。 対話に応じた6組の活動はさまざまだ。むしろ「デザイン」という領域をメインのフィールドとしているのは、ルーベン・パター（Ruben Pater）ぐらいと言ってもいいかもしれない。彼にしても『The Politics of Design』（BIS Publishers、2016）のようにデザインが孕む政治性、権力性について書いた著作があり、さまざまな活動に取り組んでいる。平山の依頼に応じたのは他にキュレーション集団、グループなど多様であり、複数のアウトプット──書店、出版、展示、社会運動など──に取り組んでいるケースが多い。 彼／彼女たちのアクチュアルで柔軟なアプローチについては実際に本を参照されたいが、印象に残ったのは女性やノンバイナリーアーティストを支援するイニシアチブのグローイング・ペインズ（Growing Pains）のメンバーが持参した文化的表象である。彼女たちが対話の起点としたのは、オランダの税務局が使用する封筒だった。 オランダでは育児給付金制度を悪用し、不正に受給した後国外逃亡した詐欺事件が2013年に発覚した。そして政府はその後、対策として「二重国籍者、主に西洋風でない姓を持つ者、そしてひとり親家庭を特に標的とするシステムを導入★3」する。AIも使われていたというこの人種差別的なシステムによって、オランダでは何千もの家族が身に覚えのない詐欺の告発にあい、給付金の返還を求められたのである。 18年にこのスキャンダルは発覚し、関与した内閣は失脚したが、人種によるプロファイリングは制度の一部に未だ残り続けているとグローイング・ペインズのジュニア・スヴェンスチンスカヤは語る。オランダの国章がビジュアルアイデンティティとして小さめに印刷され、簡素なタイポグラフィで構成されたこの税務局の封筒は、極めて事務的で「モダン」なデザインである。しかし、その背後にはアルゴリズムとして組み込まれた人種バイアスがあり、そこにある権力を──結果的に──表わしているのである。 ★1──平山みな美編『交差点で：デザイン、言語、経験』（けはい出版、2026、13ページ） ★2──同上、7ページ ★3──同上、91ページ （後編へ）※8/17公開予定 執筆日：2026/05/15（金）
